a347.speaker: A refugee from the DRC, a mother of three at the Rwamwanja Refugee Settlement (anonymous)
a347.name: A refugee from the DRC
a347.title: a mother of three at the Rwamwanja Refugee Settlement (anonymous)
a347.speech: Explained, "We fled the fighting in our village with nothing but our lives. Uganda welcomed us with open arms, and now, for the first time in months, we feel safe."

a347.speaker: A Congolese refugee who has lived in Rwamwanja for five years (anonymous)
a347.name: A Congolese refugee who has lived in Rwamwanja for five years (anonymous)
a347.speech: "The policies here have allowed me to build a life. I am able to send my children to school and even employ others from the local community. We're not just surviving, we're thriving."

a347.speaker: Senior official from the UNHCR (anonymous)
a347.name: Senior official from the UNHCR (anonymous)
a347.speech: "Uganda's generosity and leadership in refugee policy have been commendable, but the needs of both refugees and host communities are now far outstripping available resources" ; "The international community must step up to ensure Uganda can continue its role as a global leader in refugee protection and support."

a399.speaker: Femi Babafemi, NDLEA Director of Media & Advocacy (statement signed on Sunday)
a399.name: Femi Babafemi
a399.title: NDLEA Director of Media & Advocacy (statement signed on Sunday)
a399.speech: Disclosed that the arrest of five members of an international drug syndicate followed the seizure of their illicit drug consignments at the NAHCO import shed of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos. "The unravelling of the drug cartel started on Sunday 20th April when their cargo of four big suitcases arrived at the NAHCO shed on an Air Peace airline flight from Johannesburg, South Africa. After days of close monitoring and investigation, the first suspect, Umeh Chisom Peter was arrested on Wednesday 24th April after he showed up to pick two of the suitcases containing Loud, a synthetic strain of cannabis owned by a Thailand-based member of the syndicate, Obum Michael. The consignment of four parcels was concealed in false bottoms of the two suitcases, while the four suitcases contain a total of 17.6 kilograms Loud and drug candies. Another member of the syndicate, Mrs. Chiwendu Uche Ugbe whose South Africa-based husband, Aloytus Uche Ugbe sent some of the consignments, was traced to Anambra state where NDLEA officers arrested her on Saturday 27th April while attempting to collect the drug parcels sent to her by her husband. Two other suspects: Onyejakor Francis Chimezie and Naaji Valentine Chukwukere, with links to the cartel were also arrested in parts of Lagos on Monday 29th April. Their arrest led to another operation in Abia state where Mrs. Chinazo Osigwe was arrested when she was to pick up some of the parcels containing Loud and drug candies sent by her husband, Osigwe Chidiebere Anthony who is equally operating from South Africa."

a478.speaker: Fahd bin Abdulrahman Al-Jalajel, Saudi Health Minister, and Musab Nazzal Al-Ali, Syrian Health Minister
a478.name: Fahd bin Abdulrahman Al-Jalajel
a478.title: Saudi Health Minister, and Musab Nazzal Al-Ali, Syrian Health Minister
a478.speech: At their bilateral meeting they discussed the various challenges facing the Syrian health system and the possibilities for cooperation between the two countries in addressing those challenges.

a718.speaker: Abdoulaye Sanoh, Representative of Total Energies Guinea
a718.name: Abdoulaye Sanoh
a718.title: Representative of Total Energies Guinea
a718.speech: Said the aim of the tournament is to strengthen partnership ties with their clients but also to help orphans: “This tournament was organised in order to engage with our clients first, and then it has a sustainable development, CSR component, which allows us to come to the aid of a charitable cause. That is somewhat the goal, and we were able to do it. We were able to help several charitable organisations present here, to help them meet the needs of destitute children. So it is to strengthen our relations with our clients, but in the end, for that to result in humanitarian aid. Business, as they say, must have a human face. It is a non-profit tournament, to begin with. There are no winners, it is just about participating, giving joy to children. Each participating team had to choose a charity. In case of victory, it is to sponsor that charity. It is volunteer work. As I said, strengthening our relations with our clients as suppliers. But also, in the end, making a gesture for a charitable cause. That is why we organised this tournament.”

a718.speaker: Mohamed Lamine Keïta, Director of Institutional Communication and External Relations, Orange Guinea
a718.name: Mohamed Lamine Keïta
a718.title: Director of Institutional Communication and External Relations, Orange Guinea
a718.speech: Welcomed the initiative: “It is a feeling of gratitude, because this is not just a simple tournament, it is a tournament with a humanitarian purpose. The objective being to support an orphanage. That is why we took part with great pleasure, not only to combine the useful with the pleasant, but also to show that we are a responsible company, that stands alongside other companies, in order to support the most disadvantaged people.”

a718.speaker: Mamadou Mouctar Baldé, President of the orphanage of the late Ibrahima Saïkou Diallo (alias CIA)
a718.name: Mamadou Mouctar Baldé
a718.title: President of the orphanage of the late Ibrahima Saïkou Diallo (alias CIA)
a718.speech: Said the prize will be used to pay the school and health costs of the orphans: “It is a feeling of joy and satisfaction. Because Total Energies has been a good partner to our orphanage since the lifetime of our founding president, Ibrahima Saïkou Diallo, known as CIA, who maintained good relations with Total. And that is what Total continues to prove: taking care of the destitute children of Guinea. So we are truly satisfied with this prize. It can enable us to meet the Centre’s crucial needs, in particular schooling and above all the children’s health.”

a718.speaker: Moussa Camara, Captain of the winning Bonagui team
a718.name: Moussa Camara
a718.title: Captain of the winning Bonagui team
a718.speech: Reacted after the trophy presentation: “It is a great joy for us. A very great satisfaction. From the start of the tournament, we fought hard. We came to win it. We were united. We worked well to win. Today we are the winners. We are very satisfied, very happy with the trophy. We can only thank them. Wanting to launch such an event for young people, for companies, is also encouraging. And on top of that it is humanitarian. That is something we knew very well. We thank them a lot. At the next edition, we will do our best again, to win a second time.”

a752.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a752.name: John Dramani Mahama
a752.title: President of Ghana
a752.speech: Called on African leaders to take bold ownership of the continent's debt crisis, describing it as both self-inflicted and unsustainable; stressed the need for accountability, transparency, and a shift in debt governance, warning that Africa is "at a crossroads": "Africa today stands at a crossroads. On the one hand, we are witnessing commendable progress… yet access to affordable, long-term finance remains elusive."

a752.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a752.name: John Dramani Mahama
a752.title: President of Ghana
a752.speech: Lamented that in 2024, African countries spent more than $90 billion on debt servicing—"almost double the amount received in foreign aid", a burden he warned was undermining public investments in health and education.

a752.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a752.name: John Dramani Mahama
a752.title: President of Ghana
a752.speech: Referencing Ghana's experience, described how his own nation was forced into restructuring after years of unsustainable borrowing, external shocks, and poor fiscal discipline: "In Ghana, over the last several years there was an acceleration of debt accumulation, much of it going into budget support in a poor governance environment." He pointed to the lessons Ghana has learned from its recovery process, including a recent $5.4 billion debt restructuring deal under the G20 Common Framework, and emphasized the importance of leadership.

a752.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a752.name: John Dramani Mahama
a752.title: President of Ghana
a752.speech: "Sustainable debt is not just about ratios—it is about what debt finances, and the governance that underpins it." ; "And here we, leaders of Africa, must take responsibility for the debt trap we find ourselves in." ; "This is not just a technical theme—it is a call to confront one of the most defining challenges of our generation."

a752.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a752.name: John Dramani Mahama
a752.title: President of Ghana
a752.speech: Called for more flexible multilateral support aligned with domestic priorities, urging African countries to approach creditor engagement with transparency and urgency.

a845.speaker: Mohammed Abdrabuh Al-Yami, Director General of the Union of News Agencies of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (UNA)
a845.name: Mohammed Abdrabuh Al-Yami
a845.title: Director General of the Union of News Agencies of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (UNA)
a845.speech: Delivered a speech in which he addressed the relationship with the Strategic Vision Group: Russia - Islamic World and the role it has played in promoting cooperation between media institutions in the countries of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and their counterparts in the Russian Federation.

a863.speaker: News sources (unnamed)
a863.name: News sources (unnamed)
a863.speech: According to news sources, only 294 employees will remain, including 12 in the Africa Department and eight in the Asia department.

a863.speaker: Brian Atwood, former head of USAID
a863.name: Brian Atwood
a863.title: former head of USAID
a863.speech: "This decision is outrageous," he said, warning that dismissing the employees will endanger the survival of the agency, whose staff have been fighting night and day to save human lives ; "Many people will die," said Atwood, who is now a Senior Visiting Lecturer at Brown University in the United States.

a863.speaker: U.S. internal department (non-response)
a863.name: U.S. internal department (non-response)
a863.speech: Has not issued any statement regarding the claims of cutting those staff.

a863.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a863.name: Marco Rubio
a863.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a863.speech: Said that the government is continuing to carry out an assessment to look at particular programmes that should not be included in that plan, which will affect the agency.

a863.speaker: Trump administration
a863.name: Trump administration
a863.speech: Announced on Tuesday that it would place all USAID employees worldwide on compulsory leave while suspending the agency's operations.

a863.speaker: Congressional Research Service (CRS)
a863.name: Congressional Research Service (CRS)
a863.speech: According to CRS, USAID has more than 10,000 employees worldwide, two-thirds of whom (more than 7,500) work outside the United States.

a863.speaker: Reliable sources from within USAID (anonymous)
a863.name: Reliable sources from within USAID (anonymous)
a863.speech: Told Reuters that some employees have already begun to be given dismissal letters.

a863.speaker: USAID website (notice published Friday February 7)
a863.name: USAID website (notice published Friday February 7)
a863.speech: "All USAID employees are required to go on leave, except only those who oversee special administrative activities or emergency matters in special programmes." The website also said that specific employees required to continue being present in the office would be informed by Thursday at 11:00 p.m.

a931.speaker: Garmai Koboi, Director General of the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO)
a931.name: Garmai Koboi
a931.title: Director General of the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO)
a931.speech: “The enthusiasm and interest shown by the people of Nimba in understanding intellectual property were remarkable and encouraging” ; emphasized that because of Nimba's economic potential, it is home to a lot of untapped talent, which could thrive with greater awareness of IP laws and their benefits ; “We are investing in providing the knowledge the people of Nimba need to not just protect their ideas but to commercialize them as well.”

a931.speaker: Garmai Koboi, Director General of the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO)
a931.name: Garmai Koboi
a931.title: Director General of the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO)
a931.speech: “Every Liberian plays a crucial role in this effort. By respecting intellectual property rights and choosing legitimate products, we contribute to building a more vibrant economy that values and protects creativity.”

a931.speaker: Samuel Hardt, Ganta City Mayor
a931.name: Samuel Hardt
a931.title: Ganta City Mayor
a931.speech: Expressed his appreciation for LIPO's efforts, describing it as a historic moment for Nimba County, and noted that LIPO's actions are a vital step toward ensuring that creators and innovators in Nimba County receive the recognition and rewards “they deserve for their work.”

a931.speaker: Eastman (official at the Ganta event)
a931.name: Eastman (official at the Ganta event)
a931.speech: “This visit from LIPO is a pivotal milestone for our city. Educating our community about intellectual property creates opportunities for economic empowerment and the growth of our local industries.”

a958.speaker: Police investigation (Ghana Police, Adidome/Central Tongu District)
a958.name: Police investigation (Ghana Police
a958.title: Adidome/Central Tongu District)
a958.speech: The Police investigation into the ritual murder at Adidome has revealed a shocking motive behind the gruesome killing.

a958.speaker: Sources close to the investigation (anonymous)
a958.name: Sources close to the investigation (anonymous)
a958.speech: According to sources, the suspect suspected the deceased to be chasing Augustina Fiawoyipe, a young woman fetish priestess, who is also a suspect in the case.

a958.speaker: Intelligence source (anonymous)
a958.name: Intelligence source (anonymous)
a958.speech: stated that Wisdom then saw it as an opportunity to eliminate his suspected rival, Nelson Anyena ; also intimated that after receiving the amount, Courage, a popular person at Avakpokope, and the main architect, Wisdom, said to be a private security guard, resorted to affluent living.

a958.speaker: Security sources (anonymous)
a958.name: Security sources (anonymous)
a958.speech: confirmed that Augustina, the fetish priestess, intimated to them that she started smoking cannabis at a tender age and it is hard for her to stay a day without it, and that she also enjoyed the booty.

a958.speaker: Senior citizen from Adidome locality (anonymous)
a958.name: Senior citizen from Adidome locality (anonymous)
a958.speech: tried to explain the circumstances leading to the ritual murders; according to him, it is common knowledge that deities known as ‘korku’ are associated with feeding on human blood and body parts used as the foundation on which the statue deity is built ; he went on that it is not strange that people often get missing in areas and immediate communities where the deity (korku) is established.

a958.speaker: Okyehene, Amoatia Ofori Panin
a958.name: Okyehene
a958.title: Amoatia Ofori Panin
a958.speech: following the disturbing news in his traditional area, threatened to ban these foreign shrines from his kingdom.

a989.name: The Winter Cabinet Report Card (Lesotho Public Eye assessment)
a989.speech: Grading ministers from A (excellent) to U (ungraded), reveals widespread underperformance and policy failures across key government portfolios, with 12 ministers graded E or F and two ungraded due to incompetence.

a989.speaker: Nthomeng Majara, Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a989.name: Nthomeng Majara
a989.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a989.speech: Admitted that the government was “ill-prepared” upon taking office.

a989.speaker: Lesotho Workers Association
a989.name: Lesotho Workers Association
a989.speech: Made its latest call on the health minister to act on the imminent strikes by village health workers over unpaid wages (M2 448 per month) on April 29.

a989.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Minister of Trade
a989.name: Mokhethi Shelile
a989.title: Minister of Trade
a989.speech: Offers shallow assurances on pursuing alternative markets such as the EU through the AfCFTA without concrete results, and dismissed the AfDB’s EIA requirement for the M200 million Lesotho Standards Institute building, arguing that an EIA is “not standard.”

a989.speaker: Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Lesotho
a989.name: Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Lesotho
a989.speech: Recommended the dismissal of Public Works and Transport Minister Neo Matjato Moteane due to irregularities in the tender process for Moshoeshoe I International Airport’s renovation; PAC reports also reveal that Minister Limpho Tau’s company owes over M1 million in unpaid electricity to the financially struggling LEC.

a989.speaker: Neo Matjato Moteane, Minister of Public Works and Transport
a989.name: Neo Matjato Moteane
a989.title: Minister of Public Works and Transport
a989.speech: Stated that he is “ready to go if Matekane fires him.”

a989.speaker: Government Assets and Recovery Task Team
a989.name: Government Assets and Recovery Task Team
a989.speech: Claims to lack resources, raising doubts about the government’s commitment to recovering stolen assets.

a1354.speaker: Malian government and the International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1354.name: Malian government and the International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1354.speech: Have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation on migration management. During a recent meeting between Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maiga and IOM Deputy Chief of Staff Mohamed Abdiker, the two parties discussed key areas of collaboration, including revising the National Migration Policy to address current challenges and promote safe, orderly, and regular migration; IOM continuing to provide humanitarian assistance to Malian migrants in distress, including repatriation and reintegration programs; and exploring ways to harness the potential of the Malian diaspora to contribute to the country's development. Both parties agreed to work closely to address integrated border management and civil status modernization and ensure the protection of vulnerable migrants.

a1420.speaker: Nic Cheeseman, Professor of democracy at the University of Birmingham and founding director of Birmingham's Centre for Elections, Democracy, Accountability and Representation
a1420.name: Nic Cheeseman
a1420.title: Professor of democracy at the University of Birmingham and founding director of Birmingham's Centre for Elections, Democracy, Accountability and Representation
a1420.speech: Says it is a huge concern that more incumbent governments in Africa are now using high-risk strategies to rig elections, said high-risk strategies have been observed in a number of countries in Africa, one such tactic being the arrest of critics of the incumbent government including opposition leaders and members of civil society, and said these are strategies that governments cannot get away with as people are aware of what the scheme is all about ; "It is concerning that we are seeing high levels of that across the continent. It might be a signal that people think they could get away with more than they could before. What is worrying is that some of this is working across the borders. Where was Kizza Bessigye taken from? He was not arrested in Uganda. He was taken from Nairobi, Kenya. Some of this is cross-border oppression" ; responding to a question from Nation Publications Limited on whether the arrests relate to rigging, said such incidents are not new, as the case of Uganda.

a1420.speaker: Nic Cheeseman, Professor of democracy at the University of Birmingham
a1420.name: Nic Cheeseman
a1420.title: Professor of democracy at the University of Birmingham
a1420.speech: Observed that governments that feel threatened are most likely to use violence and oppression as a rigging strategy, saying it could be worse now due to, for example, the defunding of the United States Agency for International Development (USAid) ; "It is a big signal that the ruling parties are not willing to lose power. Some of this is about sending a warning. Governments that feel they can win are not as oppressive. What I see in Tanzania and Uganda are governments that feel threatened. These are governments that feel that the West and international election observers are not going to be well-funded. The defunding of USAid, the fact that democracy does not seem to be promoted is emboldening leaders to go beyond by putting more people in jail and disrupting opposition campaigns."

a1420.speaker: Nic Cheeseman, Professor of democracy at the University of Birmingham
a1420.name: Nic Cheeseman
a1420.title: Professor of democracy at the University of Birmingham
a1420.speech: During his presentation, cited as a high-risk election rigging strategy the Malawian context where correctional fluid called Tippex was used at the eleventh hour. He said: "It is at that moment when the government realises that it is not going to win and all-of-a-sudden panics, that we can see poor quality, short-term and obvious strategies."

a1420.speaker: Chrispin Mphande, Professor, political and development analyst and discussant at the webinar
a1420.name: Chrispin Mphande
a1420.title: Professor, political and development analyst and discussant at the webinar
a1420.speech: Observed that sponsored violence is another form of rigging, which he said is used by both the ruling and opposition sides. He said: "This is more common in Malawi, where parties have stronghold regions. Parties sponsor violence and warn others against campaigning in some regions. In the context of misinformation, it can come from both the opposition and government sides, each accusing the other of certain atrocities. They may not have substantive information but would create scenarios to justify that the election was not free and fair."

a1420.speaker: The Nation newspaper (Nation Publications Limited investigation)
a1420.name: The Nation newspaper (Nation Publications Limited investigation)
a1420.speech: In March this year, our sister newspaper The Nation established that the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) was set to arrest high-profile figures previously implicated in corruption scandals.

a1420.speaker: Three sources within the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) (anonymous)
a1420.name: Three sources within the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) (anonymous)
a1420.speech: Confirmed in separate interviews that the bureau has over "the past few months" been reviewing case files and secured "substantial evidence" against some former senior government officials in the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) administration for alleged corrupt practices during their time in office.

a1420.speaker: Hilary Chilomba, Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) acting director general
a1420.name: Hilary Chilomba
a1420.title: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) acting director general
a1420.speech: In a written response to our questionnaire, while refusing to share names involved and the nature of cases, confirmed the looming arrests. "It is worth noting that our investigative function is undertaken under strict confidentiality and we cannot be playing this role through the media. [But] it is not long before the so-called big fish will be caught in the nets and brought ashore. We are independent and not afraid of anyone."

a1426.speaker: Hajia Zainab Nasir Idris, wife of the Kebbi governor and state TB ambassador
a1426.name: Hajia Zainab Nasir Idris
a1426.title: wife of the Kebbi governor and state TB ambassador
a1426.speech: According to her, tuberculosis is a dangerous disease which will be difficult to treat when not detected early, therefore the need for children to come forward for diagnosis is inevitable, saying early detection leads to cure and the total prevention of the disease which is hard to treat by children from poor background.

a1426.speaker: Hajia Zainab Nasir Idris, wife of the Kebbi governor and state TB ambassador
a1426.name: Hajia Zainab Nasir Idris
a1426.title: wife of the Kebbi governor and state TB ambassador
a1426.speech: Disclosed that the week-long activities include mass campaign and sensitisations particularly in rural areas of the state where testing and treatment will run concurrently free of charge and as well to garner funds for affected poor children: "I Zainab Idris have sacrificed myself to the control and prevention of TB in the state because every child deserves proper, sound and affordable healthcare services hence our reasons to collaborate with relevant bodies to ensure the prevention and control of TB"; said the free diagnosis, sensitisations and treatment will hold in the 21 local governments in rural, semi urban and remote villages to ensure no child is missed in the all important exercise.

a1426.speaker: Hajia Zainab Nasir Idris, state TB ambassador
a1426.name: Hajia Zainab Nasir Idris
a1426.title: state TB ambassador
a1426.speech: Urged the team to seek the support of traditional rulers in the places where the testing and treatment would take place, saying nothing will succeed or possible without the support of traditional rulers.

a1476.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of the Benin Programme for the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA-Benin)
a1476.name: Simon Pierre Adovelande
a1476.title: National Coordinator of the Benin Programme for the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA-Benin)
a1476.speech: "To manage public funds one needs… maturity and responsibility."

a1476.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.name: Simon Pierre Adovelande
a1476.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.speech: On the contracts signed with SOLETANCHE BACHY and the SOGEA SATOM EMCC consortium: "We met on Tuesday 4 August to sign two contracts within the framework of the implementation of the Benin Programme for the Millennium Challenge Account. These are two large contracts that move us forward on MCA-Benin's 'Access to Markets' project, that is, in the component concerning the modernisation of the Port of Cotonou. The two contracts, the first for an amount of nearly fifteen billion and the second costing nearly twenty-three billion of our francs, correspond respectively to the first and second of the six lots established by MCA-Benin for the works to be carried out at the Port of Cotonou. Lot No. 1 concerns the extension of the existing sand-trap groyne at the port. Today the Port of Cotonou has silting problems which mean that every year we are obliged to spend more than one billion CFA francs to dredge the port basin. The infrastructure we are going to build will make it possible, over the next 30 to 40 years, to no longer have to spend so much money on dredging. The SOGEA/SATOM/EMCC consortium won this contract and must complete the infrastructure in 22 months. As for lot No. 2, it provides for the construction of two berths for ships. We are going to build two new quay berths with a total length of 600m and a depth of 12.50m (at low tide) for container ships. Through the award of this lot, MCA-Benin will develop the container unloading and storage yards. The company SOLETANCHE BACHY was awarded this contract, to be completed in 22 months."

a1476.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.name: Simon Pierre Adovelande
a1476.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.speech: On how the contracts serve the objective of boosting Benin's economy: "First, when you see the amount of the infrastructure to be built, 15 billion on one side and 23 billion on the other, you understand the scale of these works. If I take for example the extension of the groyne which prevents the silting of the port basin, we will see, from the end of the works, that all the large vessels that today cannot come to the Port of Cotonou will begin to arrive, given the ease that will have been achieved. And if in addition we increase the port's capacity with two new quay berths which will accommodate large ships, container ships, with ultra-modern loading and unloading equipment, that means that the rate of loading and unloading will be multiplied by a much higher factor than at present. That will increase the flow of traffic. There is also the fact that, in terms of delays, the operating costs of these quays will decrease at the level of port surcharges, and so it is our economy that will be boosted. Moreover, during the construction period of this infrastructure, money is already going to be injected into the national economy because these companies will use Beninese labour, will use Beninese materials and will subcontract with Beninese companies."

a1476.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.name: Simon Pierre Adovelande
a1476.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.speech: Describing the four other lots: "It is true that the investment we are going to make at the Port of Cotonou does not concern only the two contracts we signed last Tuesday. There is lot No. 3 which will implement the zoning and traffic plan at the port. When you go inside the port today, it is extremely difficult to move around. So we are going to redo all the old traffic routes, build a new road that will allow traffic to bypass via exits that will henceforth be located along the bank at the edge of the two-hundred-metre strip, which will ensure real fluidity. Through this lot, we are going to overhaul the entire lighting system inside the port, review the entire security system, the fire-fighting system so that, when there is a fire inside the port, it can be brought under control. Lot No. 4 will allow MCA-Benin to acquire, on behalf of the Port of Cotonou, new dry-bulk unloading equipment with the aim of better managing the port environment. Through lot No. 5, MCA-Benin will acquire and install at the Port of Cotonou an oceanographic monitoring station allowing the collection and analysis of data on wind, waves, water level, currents and littoral drift in the port area. Finally, equipment will be acquired through lot No. 6 with the aim of combating pollution at the Port of Cotonou. So these are all complementary investments, but there will also be investments at the level of customs, because it will be of no use to build infrastructure if the customs clearance system remains as slow as we see today. We have also earmarked resources to modernise the entire goods clearance procedure, which will speed up the release of goods. It is a whole set of works that is going to be carried out at the Port of Cotonou."

a1476.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.name: Simon Pierre Adovelande
a1476.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.speech: Reassuring sceptical Beninese about the use of the funds: "Regarding the Beninese, there are two things I would like to stress. The first is that many people accuse MCA-Benin of doing a lot of studies. But without the studies we could not have the results we have today. And you have to take the time to respect the procedures, to carry out procurement in the greatest transparency so that in the end there is no dispute. The second thing, on the subject of the use of resources, is that the largest amounts are reserved for the works. So there are concerns among those who do not know how the programme works. Today, when we sign the contracts, that increases the disbursement amounts. By the end of October 2009, we will have committed nearly 80% of the 307 million US dollars and we will be two years from the end of the Programme. Which means there is no cause for concern about the use of the 307 million US dollars. So what I can say to the Beninese today is that we received 307 million US dollars which are tied to activities we have selected, and this amount will be entirely used. I would even say that for certain activities we will need additional resources to be able to carry them out. I am very pleased today about what we have just done, because signing contracts of such amounts in our context, that is to say that of developing countries, is not an easy thing; we achieved it and I thank the whole team that worked with me to do it because I am only the spokesman of a team. It is the result of this whole team that we are displaying today and we are proud to do so."

a1476.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.name: Simon Pierre Adovelande
a1476.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.speech: On the process that led to the selection of the winning companies: "First it must be said that the contracts we are talking about will be paid out of public funds, and to manage public funds, two things must be permanently present in the minds of those who manage those funds: maturity and responsibility. The maturity to know that one is a steward and not the owner of the funds, and the responsibility that is linked to respecting procedures. And that is our leitmotiv. Sometimes it takes time but you have to take the necessary time to do things properly. In the process that led to the signing of these contracts, we began back in July 2008 when we launched the calls for tender. There was previously a pre-qualification phase at the end of which companies were shortlisted. These companies were treated in the same way, the same information was given to them at the same time, and site visits were carried out at the same time. It must be said that MCA-Benin is not the only member of this selection panel, which brought together all the actors involved, and the results can be consulted on the internet. Today we have already signed more than six hundred contracts at MCA-Benin without a single dispute. We have already committed more than one hundred billion CFA francs and we have not had a single dispute because maturity and responsibility were present."

a1476.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.name: Simon Pierre Adovelande
a1476.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a1476.speech: On the timetable for the remaining contracts: "We are going to sign, during the month of September–October of this year 2009, the third lot, which amounts to a little more than 40 million US dollars, or about 18 billion CFA francs. The other contracts, that is to say lot 4, lot 5 and lot 6, will be signed by December. In the same momentum, we are going to move on to the Access to Justice Project where we will have to build eight courts of first instance, the Abomey Court of Appeal and the Legal Documentation Centre. And there we also have nearly 20 billion francs of contracts to sign and all these contracts will be signed before December of this year 2009. I would like, in conclusion, to recall that MCA-Benin, as I always say, is a five-year programme and you cannot have the results of the fifth year in the first or second year; let us wait for the fifth year and we will all be happy to see the infrastructure that is planned."

a1568.speaker: António Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a1568.name: António Guterres
a1568.title: Secretary-General of the United Nations
a1568.speech: Reaffirmed the UN's commitment to supporting Niger in its efforts to meet the economic and social challenges it faces.

a1568.speaker: Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, Prime Minister and Minister of the Economy and Finance of Niger
a1568.name: Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine
a1568.title: Prime Minister and Minister of the Economy and Finance of Niger
a1568.speech: First offered his congratulations to the head of the UN on the 80th anniversary of the organisation's creation. He then stressed that, since the advent of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP), the Nigerien people have chosen to take charge of their own destiny by relying first on their own means. He also noted that cooperation between Niger and the UN has been strengthened thanks to better alignment of UN projects with the government's priorities, organised around four flagship programmes: socio-economic governance; education and training; youth and employability; and food sovereignty.

a1568.speaker: Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, Prime Minister of Niger
a1568.name: Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine
a1568.title: Prime Minister of Niger
a1568.speech: Turning to the security situation, recalled that Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali have decided to pool their military resources and intelligence capabilities in order to fight, with determination, against the terrorism afflicting the Sahel.

a1617.speaker: Management of the Ghana Gold Board (GOLDBOD)
a1617.name: Management of the Ghana Gold Board (GOLDBOD)
a1617.speech: Has announced the Board's target of $12 billion annually in gold revenue starting next year, as it aims to increase its weekly gold purchases from 1.5 tonnes (in January) to over three tonnes by year-end.

a1617.speaker: Economists
a1617.name: Economists
a1617.speech: Described the $10 billion "Big Push" as "one of the most comprehensive blueprints for tackling the country's deep-rooted structural challenges."

a1617.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1617.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1617.title: President of Ghana
a1617.speech: Promised, in the rail and urban transit sector, to revitalise the Eastern and Western rail corridors and introduce light rail systems in Accra, Kumasi and Takoradi, and, in the WASH sector, made promises to people in under-served cities and towns, namely Ho, Tamale and Yendi; his shopping list included dualisation of critical highways such as Accra-Kumasi, Accra-Aflao and Accra-Takoradi, coupled with the construction of bridges and rural feeder roads.

a1680.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a1680.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a1680.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a1680.speech: Asked the newly presented administrator of Kiremba commune to serve as a model and to use his leadership to steer the commune towards Burundi's emergence in 2040 and development in 2060. Recalling that an authority is the symbol of the unity of the people, he recommended that he unite the population and guide it in development projects, work in common effort with the population, always listen to their grievances, and enlighten the population to fight against fraud, corruption and all forms of economic malpractice.

a1680.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a1680.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a1680.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a1680.speech: Congratulated the population of Kiremba commune for having taken first place in the promotion of avocado cultivation, which will help the Burundian community boost exports as well as the foreign currency entering the country.

a1680.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a1680.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a1680.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a1680.speech: Said Burundi went through a period of disorder that disrupted development, and that the pooling of efforts remains necessary; to achieve development everyone's talent must be harnessed by coming together for mutual aid and complementarity. He stressed that it is also necessary to avoid all forms of division and to increase working hours in order to build a better future for the country, adding that since 2005 Burundi has progressed thanks to the unity and solidarity of Burundians, and calling on the people of Kiremba to remember their past in order to preserve what has been achieved and guide the future.

a1680.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a1680.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a1680.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a1680.speech: Called on religious leaders to teach their faithful to roll up their sleeves, apply themselves to development activities and contribute to the country's development, recommending that they mobilise Christians to work in cooperatives and contribute to increasing production.

a1680.speaker: Pascal Habiyakare, administrator of Kiremba commune
a1680.name: Pascal Habiyakare
a1680.title: administrator of Kiremba commune
a1680.speech: Pledged to work in close collaboration with the people, to fight with all his energy against every form of injustice and to advocate for the well-being of the population. He requested from the population support centred on bravery in development activities.

a1718.speaker: Isaac Chamba, TAWA Wildlife Conservation Officer
a1718.name: Isaac Chamba
a1718.title: TAWA Wildlife Conservation Officer
a1718.speech: Speaking recently at a workshop organised by the Journalists' Environmental Association of Tanzania (JET) in Bagamoyo, Coast Region, said conflicts were relatively minor until 2018, when incidents surged, prompting the Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism to develop the National Human-Wildlife Conflict Management Strategy (2020-2024). He outlined several strategic objectives, such as enhancing community-based mitigation, establishing effective HWC response mechanisms, managing the human-wildlife interface and promoting the benefits of coexistence. "We have launched awareness campaigns to highlight the ecological and economic advantages of wildlife, aiming to foster positive attitudes and encourage protective measures among farmers," he explained.

a1718.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a1718.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a1718.title: President of Tanzania
a1718.speech: During her visit to Tunduru District in the Ruvuma Region, addressed the issue of human-wildlife conflict, particularly concerning crop destruction by elephants. She directed TAWA to enhance efforts to promote coexistence, assuring residents that the government is taking steps to resolve the issue, including increasing ranger numbers and introducing drones for monitoring. The president emphasised the importance of community engagement, stating, "It is crucial for the government to involve local communities in wildlife conservation efforts, which includes educating farmers about coexistence strategies and the significance of wildlife conservation." She supported community-based approaches that empower locals to manage wildlife resources sustainably, providing training and resources to help them protect their crops.

a1718.speaker: Hassan Zidadu Kungu, Tunduru North Member of Parliament
a1718.name: Hassan Zidadu Kungu
a1718.title: Tunduru North Member of Parliament
a1718.speech: Pointed out the ongoing challenges of crop damage, conflicts between farmers and herders and pesticide availability. While he acknowledged government efforts, he stressed that more needs to be done.

a1718.speaker: Ambassador Dr Emmanuel Nchimbi, CCM Secretary General
a1718.name: Ambassador Dr Emmanuel Nchimbi
a1718.title: CCM Secretary General
a1718.speech: In a related directive, instructed the Minister for Natural Resources and Tourism, Dr Pindi Chana, to ensure conservation officers effectively manage wild animals, including elephants and hippopotamuses, that invade local farms.

a1718.speaker: Mabula Nyanda, TAWA Commissioner for Conservation
a1718.name: Mabula Nyanda
a1718.title: TAWA Commissioner for Conservation
a1718.speech: Announced that four DJI Mavic 3 drones will be deployed to monitor affected districts.

a1732.speaker: Michal Makocki, Senior Associate Fellow at the EU Institute of Security Studies (EUISS)
a1732.name: Michal Makocki
a1732.title: Senior Associate Fellow at the EU Institute of Security Studies (EUISS)
a1732.speech: Stated that the EU's development agenda is increasingly driven by security and migration concerns; that in turn China's security engagement is motivated by the need to protect its fast-growing economic interests on the continent; and that this makes the EU's and China's starting points closer than in 2008, when the triangular cooperation was first suggested, given the importance of sustained high economic growth for Africa's stability ; noted that extending the EU-China Dialogue on Security and Defence beyond military circles to include development agencies could facilitate better coordination of different aspects of bilateral cooperation.

a1732.speaker: Michal Makocki, Senior Associate Fellow at the EU Institute of Security Studies (EUISS)
a1732.name: Michal Makocki
a1732.title: Senior Associate Fellow at the EU Institute of Security Studies (EUISS)
a1732.speech: According to Michal Makocki, the EU could appropriate grants to support local governments' feasibility studies for Chinese investments to better gauge their impact in terms of economic potential but also to better address potential negative externalities; the result would be sustainable economic growth and stability, two of the key factors for addressing the root causes of migration.

a1732.speaker: Jakob Bund, Junior Analyst at the EU Institute of Security Studies (EUISS)
a1732.name: Jakob Bund
a1732.title: Junior Analyst at the EU Institute of Security Studies (EUISS)
a1732.speech: Stated that concerted efforts with the African Union to reinforce local frameworks for environmental protection, labour laws and open public procurement schemes can benefit all investors; and that, given its endeavours to strengthen good governance and support for institution and capacity building on the continent, the EU could seek to further harness oversight mechanisms that ensure transparency and accountability.

a1733.speaker: Lloyd Jackson, USAID representative in Djibouti
a1733.name: Lloyd Jackson
a1733.title: USAID representative in Djibouti
a1733.speech: Reported on all the programmes relating to education, youth and employability that he had carried out or intended to carry out with his partners; and expressed the wish to establish a privileged partnership with the Ministry of Youth and Culture (MJC), which could serve as a coordination point between USAID and the other departments.

a1733.speaker: Hibo Moumin Assoweh, Djiboutian Minister of Youth and Culture
a1733.name: Hibo Moumin Assoweh
a1733.title: Djiboutian Minister of Youth and Culture
a1733.speech: Thanked her guest for this visit and above all for this collaboration, which would open new prospects for the socio-professional integration of young people; and insisted on a number of points relating to the promotion of books, support for equipment, training and the restoration of cultural heritage, which she wished to see appear in the broad outlines of the future partnership.

a1895.speaker: Zimbabwe Livelihoods Assessment Committee (ZimLAC) report on rural livelihoods, chaired by the country's Food and Nutrition Council
a1895.name: Zimbabwe Livelihoods Assessment Committee (ZimLAC) report on rural livelihoods
a1895.title: chaired by the country's Food and Nutrition Council
a1895.speech: According to the latest ZimLAC report, Zimbabwe has for the past five years held steady at about 25% of the rural population with no access to toilets, down from 30% at the turn of the century, but the numbers have not improved in some time. About half of Zimbabwe's rural population have access to basic toilets and another 9% have access to limited toilets. Matabeleland North has the worst open defecation rate at 50%, and within that province the district of Binga recorded a 73% rate; in Lupane 53% of residents have no access to toilets. According to the report, only 6% of households have hand washing stations.

a1895.speaker: Zimbabwe Livelihoods Assessment Committee (ZimLAC)
a1895.name: Zimbabwe Livelihoods Assessment Committee (ZimLAC)
a1895.speech: Said Zimbabwe has gone backwards in the past year at the level of overall basic water services, with the level of access declining from 60% in 2023 to 52% in 2024.

a1895.speaker: Local media (Zimbabwe)
a1895.name: Local media (Zimbabwe)
a1895.speech: Reported that before the five-year USAID programme to build toilets in Nkayi, residents didn't know the importance of having toilets.

a1895.speaker: Bahle Makhalima, resident of Nkayi, Matabeleland North
a1895.name: Bahle Makhalima
a1895.title: resident of Nkayi, Matabeleland North
a1895.speech: "We took pride in going to the bush. As women here, we lacked knowledge on the importance of having a toilet at home," she told journalists.

a1907.speaker: NBC (citing unnamed officials)
a1907.name: NBC (citing unnamed officials)
a1907.speech: Reported on Saturday that the US could send troops to guard Ukraine's rare earth minerals, which it wants as repayment for American aid.

a1907.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1907.name: Donald Trump
a1907.title: US President
a1907.speech: Demanded the "equivalent of $500 billion worth of rare earths" from Ukraine in exchange for what he estimated to be "more than $300 billion" Washington had provided in aid since the escalation of Kiev's conflict with Moscow in 2022.

a1907.speaker: Four officials who spoke to NBC (anonymous)
a1907.name: Four officials who spoke to NBC (anonymous)
a1907.speech: Said the proposed contract also signaled Washington's intention to deploy American troops to the sites as a protection detail, and that the deployment could reportedly come after Russia and Ukraine reached a deal to end the ongoing conflict.

a1907.speaker: Pete Hegseth, US Defense Secretary
a1907.name: Pete Hegseth
a1907.title: US Defense Secretary
a1907.speech: Speaking at a gathering of Kiev's supporters in Brussels earlier this week, ruled out sending American forces there following any security deal.

a1907.speaker: J.D. Vance, US Vice President
a1907.name: J.D. Vance
a1907.title: US Vice President
a1907.speech: In an interview with The Wall Street Journal on Thursday, indicated that the possibility of sending American troops to Ukraine remained "on the table" if Moscow refused to engage in good-faith negotiations.

a1907.speaker: Vladimir Zelensky, Ukrainian leader
a1907.name: Vladimir Zelensky
a1907.title: Ukrainian leader
a1907.speech: Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference on Saturday, said the US proposal so far lacked "security guarantees" for Kiev and was not "in the interests of sovereign Ukraine" ; "For me it is very important that there is a connection between some kind of security guarantees and some kind of investment… If we want to sign something we have to understand that it will work and it will be very positive for both nations" ; indicated that the document Bessent presented to him will need to be amended to reflect Ukraine's interests, noting he would like to have a mutually beneficial partnership with the US as opposed to simply giving his country's natural resources away.

a1907.speaker: Vladimir Zelensky, Ukrainian leader
a1907.name: Vladimir Zelensky
a1907.title: Ukrainian leader
a1907.speech: Recently admitted that a large chunk of Ukraine's mineral-rich territories, some 20%, is currently under Russian control.

a1907.speaker: Ukraine's Institute of Geology
a1907.name: Ukraine's Institute of Geology
a1907.speech: According to Ukraine's Institute of Geology, the country's deposits include lanthanum, cerium, neodymium, erbium and yttrium.

a2360.speaker: Resident of the Tira-Chapeu neighbourhood, Praia
a2360.name: Resident of the Tira-Chapeu neighbourhood
a2360.title: Praia
a2360.speech: Reports that "The children must reduce their trips to the bathroom", her house having been a month without water from the public network.

a2360.speaker: Aguas de Santiago (AdS)
a2360.name: Aguas de Santiago (AdS)
a2360.speech: Complains of a chronic difficulty in being unable to bill for more than half the water in the network, because of clandestine connections, collection difficulties and losses in the pipes.

a2360.speaker: Lucia Barros, 47, resident of Praia
a2360.name: Lucia Barros
a2360.title: 47, resident of Praia
a2360.speech: Said her three children have to wear "the same clothes at least twice" and lamented to Lusa: "My house is dirty and for a month I have only been sweeping, without running a [wet] cloth over the floor" ; said she buys 200 litres of water at a time from tanker trucks for 320 escudos, but because it has "a yellowish colour" she only uses it to "clean the floor and the toilet."

a2360.speaker: Bernardina Moreira, 79, resident of Praia
a2360.name: Bernardina Moreira
a2360.title: 79, resident of Praia
a2360.speech: Protests that she has gone 16 days without receiving water from the public network, a record since she has lived in that area of the capital: "The water used to come every three days," she recalls.

a2360.speaker: Josefa da Veiga, 62, resident of the Eugenio Lima neighbourhood
a2360.name: Josefa da Veiga
a2360.title: 62, resident of the Eugenio Lima neighbourhood
a2360.speech: Said that a week ago she spent an entire night in the yard waiting for a drop of water, which spurted out for a few minutes on the ground floor and filled only 10-litre containers, and said that December was the last time the water rose to the third floor and filled the one-tonne tank.

a2360.speaker: Nilton Fonseca, municipal council employee and private water supplier
a2360.name: Nilton Fonseca
a2360.title: municipal council employee and private water supplier
a2360.speech: Says he receives "more than 100 calls" a day, but cannot respond to them all.

a2360.speaker: Nilton Duarte, president of the public company Aguas de Santiago (AdS)
a2360.name: Nilton Duarte
a2360.title: president of the public company Aguas de Santiago (AdS)
a2360.speech: Explained that the public company Electra, which is responsible for water capture, does not supply enough water for the company to distribute: AdS receives 12,000 cubic metres of water per day, but would need more than 15,000 to normalise supply and compensate for losses and theft ; said the problem in Praia will only be solved when Electra supplies more water and that they are in talks with the shareholder, the State.

a2360.speaker: Nilton Duarte, president of the public company Aguas de Santiago (AdS)
a2360.name: Nilton Duarte
a2360.title: president of the public company Aguas de Santiago (AdS)
a2360.speech: Complained that theft of water from the public network through clandestine connections is a frequent practice in the capital because there are no penalties, becoming a problem for the sustainability of the distribution company; reported that teams install the network but "often" residents ignore the meter "because they say they are going to steal afterwards"; asked the Government to take to parliament a law to criminalise clandestine connections, similar to the September 2014 law that made electricity theft a crime; said that as long as there are no measures two scenarios will prevail in Praia, "many people without water" and residents who "clearly say" that they make their own connections; reaffirmed that the company cannot bill for more than half of the water in the network, and insisted: "And we can do nothing. This is the situation we are in and we appeal to the competent authorities to help us."

a2360.speaker: Nilton Duarte, president of the public company Aguas de Santiago (AdS)
a2360.name: Nilton Duarte
a2360.title: president of the public company Aguas de Santiago (AdS)
a2360.speech: Said a "contingency plan" is under way to rationalise distribution with set timetables for each zone, "so that everyone can have water"; said there are no neighbourhoods with more than 15 days without water, but acknowledged that there may be houses with problems in the pipes or poor location of storage cisterns, which should be at ground level so that network pressure can reach them.

a2360.speaker: AdS annual reports
a2360.name: AdS annual reports
a2360.speech: Have stated that the company cannot bill for more than half of the water in the network, because of clandestine connections, collection difficulties and losses in the pipes.

a2383.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a2383.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
a2383.title: President of Namibia
a2383.speech: Expressed deep sadness over the passing of Pope Francis, describing him as an extraordinary leader who served the world with compassion, courage and integrity. In a statement issued following the pope’s death, she said humanity had lost a strong spiritual leader who will be remembered for his dedication to helping those in need and his efforts to bring attention to global socio-economic challenges, especially in developing countries. “Since he became head of the Vatican in 2013 as the first pope from the global south, Pope Francis brought attention to the struggles of the poor and the developing world,” the President said ; She added that his passing, which comes during the holy Easter period, is a reminder for everyone to continue working towards a just and fair world, especially for vulnerable communities ; “We shall forever recall his simplicity and the wise spiritual guidance he emphasized in dealing with the challenges facing humanity,” she said ; On behalf of the Namibian people and government, she offered condolences to the Vatican, the global Catholic Church and the late Pope’s family: “May the soul of Pope Francis rest in eternal peace.”

a2546.speaker: Ordinance of 14 October 2024 signed by Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP)
a2546.name: Ordinance of 14 October 2024 signed by Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani
a2546.title: President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP)
a2546.speech: Determines the derogatory tax regime applicable to the importation, production and marketing of CEM II 32.5 grey cement, granting numerous exemptions to companies duly established in Niger and engaged in the importation, production and marketing of grey cement.

a2546.speaker: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger (arrete/decree)
a2546.name: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger (arrete/decree)
a2546.speech: Set, by decree, ceiling prices for a tonne of CEM II 32.5 grey cement applicable in the country's eight regions: 55,000 FCFA in Niamey; 56,000 F in Dosso; 51,000 F in Tahoua; 57,000 F in Maradi; 58,000 F in Zinder; and 59,000 F in Diffa, Agadez and Tillaberi.

a2737.speaker: Israeli Ministry of Defense (post on the social network X)
a2737.name: Israeli Ministry of Defense (post on the social network X)
a2737.speech: Wrote that 120 trucks entered the Gaza Strip and that the United Nations (UN) and other non-governmental organisations distributed food to the Palestinian population during a limited “tactical pause” in its military operations.

a2737.speaker: Government of Hamas (cited by the news agency Efe)
a2737.name: Government of Hamas (cited by the news agency Efe)
a2737.speech: Said that only 73 trucks entered the Gaza Strip, “most of which were looted under the watchful eye of the Israeli occupation and its drones, in a clear attempt to prevent the aid from reaching the distribution centres” ; according to Hamas, three air-drop aid operations were also carried out which “represented no more than the equivalent of two trucks” and whose supplies fell in areas considered combat zones by the Israeli army and inaccessible to civilians for security reasons.

a2737.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2737.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2737.speech: Has warned of the “alarming levels” of malnutrition in the Gaza Strip and that the “deliberate blockade” of humanitarian aid has already cost the lives of many Palestinians.

a2737.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2737.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2737.speech: According to the WHO, in Gaza almost 20% of children under five are currently acutely malnourished; during the first two weeks of July more than 5,000 children under five received outpatient treatment for malnutrition – 18% of whom suffered from the most life-threatening form, severe acute malnutrition.

a2737.speaker: Egyptian state television channels (Al Qahera News and ExtraNews)
a2737.name: Egyptian state television channels (Al Qahera News and ExtraNews)
a2737.speech: Reported on Sunday that “dozens of Egyptian trucks with humanitarian aid began to leave the Egyptian side of the Rafah crossing heading for the Gaza Strip” ; “The trucks are carrying large quantities of food, flour and essential supplies for infrastructure, as part of Egypt’s continuing efforts to alleviate the worsening humanitarian crisis in the Strip.”

a2737.speaker: Israeli army
a2737.name: Israeli army
a2737.speech: Announced today a daily 10-hour “tactical pause” in its military activities in three areas of the enclave to allow the distribution of humanitarian aid “every day until further notice,” in the face of an alarming increase in deaths from malnutrition in the Gaza Strip.

a2737.speaker: Government of Gaza
a2737.name: Government of Gaza
a2737.speech: Warned on Saturday that if powdered milk and nutritional supplements do not enter in the coming days, more than 100,000 children in Gaza risk dying of malnutrition.

a2824.speaker: Public Diplomacy Section, U.S. Consulate General in Lagos (statement)
a2824.name: Public Diplomacy Section
a2824.title: U.S. Consulate General in Lagos (statement)
a2824.speech: Said that Swart “is the senior U.S. Governments representative to the Nigerian people throughout the 17 states in southern Nigeria” ; “He is responsible for leading and overseeing U.S. government's activities that deepen trade and investment ties, expand people-to-people connections, and advance the full range of priorities in the U.S.-Nigeria bilateral relationship across the region.” ; “Swart takes over from JoEllen Gorg, who led the Consulate General in an interim capacity over the last seven months.”

a2824.speaker: Rick Swart, U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a2824.name: Rick Swart
a2824.title: U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a2824.speech: “I am honored to serve in Nigeria” ; “I am excited about the opportunity to travel across the region, meet the people, experience the culture, while advancing the shared goals of making our two countries safer, stronger, and more prosperous” ; “I thank JoEllen for her remarkable leadership and for the outstanding work she has done to promote our close partnership with the Nigerian people in the region” ; “I look forward to working closely with Ambassador Mills and the team at the U.S. Embassy in Abuja, to further advance the shared objectives between Nigeria and the United States.”

a2925.speaker: 102 non-governmental organisations (joint statement, including the Portuguese Platform of Non-Governmental Development Organisations – ONGD)
a2925.name: 102 non-governmental organisations (joint statement
a2925.title: including the Portuguese Platform of Non-Governmental Development Organisations – ONGD)
a2925.speech: Expressed “alarm and repudiation” at Israel’s threat to ban the major international humanitarian aid organisations from Gaza, and stated that despite claims by the Israeli authorities that there is no limit on the entry of humanitarian aid into Gaza, “most of the major international non-governmental organisations have not managed to deliver a single truck of vital goods since 2 March” ; “Instead of unblocking the growing volume of accumulated goods, the Israeli authorities have rejected requests from dozens of NGOs to send essential supplies, claiming that these organisations ‘are not authorised to provide aid’.”

a2925.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), which released the document
a2925.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2925.title: which released the document
a2925.speech: Added that in July alone more than 60 requests were refused on these grounds, and warned that this obstruction has left goods worth several million dollars, including food, medicines, water and shelter items, held in warehouses in Jordan and Egypt while the Palestinian population faces hunger.

a2925.speaker: Sean Carroll, president and chief executive of American Near East Refugee Aid (ANERA)
a2925.name: Sean Carroll
a2925.title: president and chief executive of American Near East Refugee Aid (ANERA)
a2925.speech: “American Near East Refugee Aid (ANERA) has more than seven million dollars in vital goods prevented from entering Gaza, including 744 pallets of rice, enough for six million meals, blocked in Ashdod, a few kilometres away.”

a2925.speaker: The 102 signatory organisations
a2925.name: The 102 signatory organisations
a2925.speech: Called on all states and donors to pressure Israel to end the instrumentalisation of aid, including through bureaucratic obstacles such as NGO registration procedures: “Help ensure that NGOs are not forced to share sensitive personal information, in violation of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), nor to compromise the safety or independence of their staff as a condition for providing aid” ; demanded the “immediate and unconditional opening” of all land crossings and conditions for the delivery of vital humanitarian aid.

a2925.speaker: United Nations
a2925.name: United Nations
a2925.speech: Has warned of a situation of widespread famine in the enclave, where Israel blocked the entry of humanitarian aid for months.

a2925.speaker: European Union and humanitarian organisations
a2925.name: European Union and humanitarian organisations
a2925.speech: Complain that the quantity of aid allowed in is insufficient to meet the needs of the population of more than two million people.

a2925.speaker: Local authorities of the Gaza Strip (controlled by Hamas)
a2925.name: Local authorities of the Gaza Strip (controlled by Hamas)
a2925.speech: Report more than 200 deaths, about half of them children, from hunger and malnutrition.

a3216.speaker: US Supreme Court (order)
a3216.name: US Supreme Court (order)
a3216.speech: Said on Friday that US President Donald Trump’s administration may continue with its freeze of over $4 billion (€3.4 billion) in foreign aid ; said that the “asserted harms” to Trump’s conduct of foreign affairs “appear to outweigh the potential harm” faced by potential recipients of the foreign aid ; said the emergency order is not a “final determination” on the freeze, as it plays out in the lower courts ; “The relief granted by the Court today reflects our preliminary view, consistent with the standards for interim relief.”

a3216.speaker: US District Judge Amir Ali
a3216.name: US District Judge Amir Ali
a3216.speech: Ruled the Trump administration must release the aid.

a3216.speaker: Liberal Justices Elena Kagan, Sonia Sotomayor, and Ketanji Brown Jackson
a3216.name: Liberal Justices Elena Kagan
a3216.title: Sonia Sotomayor, and Ketanji Brown Jackson
a3216.speech: Dissented from the Supreme Court order.

a3216.speaker: Elena Kagan, US Supreme Court Justice
a3216.name: Elena Kagan
a3216.title: US Supreme Court Justice
a3216.speech: Shot back at the Trump administration, which she ascertains does not want to spend the money because it is “contrary to US foreign policy” ; “But that is just the price of living under a Constitution that gives Congress the power to make spending decisions through the enactment of appropriations law” ; said the result of the emergency order conflicts with the “separation of powers”.

a3216.speaker: The White House
a3216.name: The White House
a3216.speech: Has often criticized aid programs which it sees as a waste of money or contrary to the aims of US foreign policy.

a3216.speaker: Researchers and humanitarian groups
a3216.name: Researchers and humanitarian groups
a3216.speech: Have warned that the aid cuts will have dire consequences for people in developing countries and global public health.

a3216.speaker: Study by the Fielding School of Public Health at the University of California, Los Angeles (released in July)
a3216.name: Study by the Fielding School of Public Health at the University of California
a3216.title: Los Angeles (released in July)
a3216.speech: Said that the cuts could result in more than 14 million additional global deaths by 2030.

a3216.speaker: International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a3216.name: International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a3216.speech: Noted that the slashing of US foreign aid includes the decision to end programs that treat and prevent communicable diseases ; “Without prevention and treatment efforts, diseases are more likely to spread unchecked, mutate and become harder to control. This creates a higher risk for future global health crises that could threaten lives worldwide,” the IRC said on its website in March.

a3410.speaker: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria (speaking through his representative, Minister of Labour and Employment Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi)
a3410.name: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria (speaking through his representative
a3410.title: Minister of Labour and Employment Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi)
a3410.speech: Hailed Nigerian workers, acknowledging their roles in nation building, noting that their dedication and resilience drive the engine of the Nigerian economy; said his felicitations and gratitude go to the hardworking men and women of the country, describing them as the backbone of our society; also sent felicitations to the leadership of the NLC and TUC for their tireless efforts in organising this year's May Day celebrations: "Your efforts and sacrifices have not only uplifted the lives of your members but have also contributed to the betterment of our society. As we mark this day, let us reaffirm our shared commitment to a nation where workers are safe, empowered, and have the freedom to actively participate in shaping the future of our country. This administration stands ready to collaborate with labour unions, the organised and informal private sector, and civil society organisations to create policies and programmes that safeguard the rights and livelihoods of workers across all sectors of the economy."

a3410.speaker: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria (speaking through his representative, Minister of Labour and Employment Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi)
a3410.name: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria (speaking through his representative
a3410.title: Minister of Labour and Employment Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi)
a3410.speech: On the theme 'Reclaiming the Civic Space in the Midst of Economic Hardship', said it speaks to the challenges we face as a nation and the opportunities that lie ahead: "Economic hardship, which today is a global phenomenon, cuts across all regions, testing the resolve of world leaders, but has not broken our spirit. I am well aware of the peculiarities of this economic hardship for Nigerians... ranging from rising costs of living, hunger, insecurity, unemployment, loss of livelihoods and the pressure to provide necessities for your families... my administration is not only committed but intentional in formulating and implementing policies that promote job creation, decent jobs, poverty alleviation, economic growth and stability, as well as supporting the most vulnerable among us." ; "We must also reclaim the civic space... A vibrant civic space is the cornerstone of democracy... Therefore, to reclaim this space, we must prioritise transparency, inclusivity, equity and dialogue. We must protect the rights of workers to organise, advocate, and participate in decision-making processes."

a3410.speaker: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria (speaking through his representative, Minister of Labour and Employment Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi)
a3410.name: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria (speaking through his representative
a3410.title: Minister of Labour and Employment Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi)
a3410.speech: Pledged that his government will continue to strengthen labour protections, improve job security, and ensure fair treatment for all workers in line with international best practices, and to address issues of underemployment: "Nigeria is at the verge of signing onto the Global Coalition for Social Justice of the International Labour Organisation to ensure that Nigeria's Labour Administration System not only resonates with best practice, but Nigeria's voice is clearly heard in the international arena of the world of work." ; "this administration shall continue to effect positive changes in the lives of the average Nigerians... and most importantly to fight the intense pain of corruption which has enriched the very few to the detriment of the majority of our citizens."

a3410.speaker: Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC) - Joe Ajaero of the NLC and Festus Osifo of the TUC
a3410.name: Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC) - Joe Ajaero of the NLC and Festus Osifo of the TUC
a3410.speech: Criticised the economic restructuring of the Bola Tinubu administration, saying in almost two years the policies have failed to address rising inflation, unemployment, exchange rate instability, among others; claimed the economic restructuring is worsening living conditions for the masses and that the numbers indicated in the nation's GDP are not adding up and do not reflect the reality on the ground: "The Nigerian economy is facing severe structural challenges, with deteriorating macroeconomic fundamentals negatively impacting workers, the real sector, and citizens' welfare... The numbers are not adding up and do not reflect the reality on the ground." ; "Whatsoever statistics or numbers that do not demonstrate that the people are well off... is sheer juju and a waste of time." ; "Inflation rate surged to 33.69%, the highest in 28 years. Food inflation 40.53%... real wages have collapsed as our purchasing power are continuously eroded, with the minimum wage of (N70,000) now worth less than N15,000 in 2019 terms." ; regretted that about 60 multinational firms (e.g., GlaxoSmithKline, P&G) exited the economy between 2023 and now due to the harsh operating environment, and advised that no economy can make progress without a strong domestic manufacturing base ; "The truth is that our economy is fiscally and monetarily challenged... Kowtowing to the wishes of neoliberal driven Bretton-wood institutions (WB/IMF) will continue to recycle hardship in our nation." ; "The ongoing tariff war sparked by President Trump's imposition of severe tariff regime on all manners of imports into the US should remind those that run our economy of the severe imperfection of the neo-liberal model."

a3410.speaker: Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC) - Joe Ajaero of the NLC and Festus Osifo of the TUC
a3410.name: Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC) - Joe Ajaero of the NLC and Festus Osifo of the TUC
a3410.speech: Blamed the Federal Government for the continuous neglect in the energy sector, saying it has consistently failed to consult stakeholders in its effort to find lasting solution to challenges in the sector: "We talk about the energy sector, yet those that claim to know better have refused to listen but insist on listening to what does not work." ; said they who are workers in the various organisations running the petroleum and power sectors know where the skeletons are buried: "We know what works."

a3410.speaker: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Human Development Index
a3410.name: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Human Development Index
a3410.speech: Cited by labour as ranking Nigeria 161 out of 193 nations sampled in the Human Development Index, classified amongst countries with low human development.

a3410.speaker: World Bank
a3410.name: World Bank
a3410.speech: Has predicted increasing poverty in Nigeria; estimates youth unemployment at over 40 percent and predicts worsening poverty and hardship amongst Nigerians as the country heads towards 2027.

a3410.speaker: Global Hunger Index (2023 report)
a3410.name: Global Hunger Index (2023 report)
a3410.speech: According to the 2023 report of the Global Hunger Index, Nigeria was ranked 109th out of 125.

a3410.speaker: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS)
a3410.name: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS)
a3410.speech: Puts underemployment at 12.6 percent, against labour's estimate of nearly 70 percent.

a3460.speaker: Constitution of the New Patriotic Party (NPP)
a3460.name: Constitution of the New Patriotic Party (NPP)
a3460.speech: The aims and objectives enshrined in the Constitution of the NPP include: “To manage the economy of the country with efficiency and prudence, guided by the consideration of national interest”; “To promote a vibrant, free-market economy and encourage vigorous participation by citizens in economic activities”; “To create a climate in which private enterprise will thrive and citizens and foreigners alike may invest without fear and without unnecessary bureaucratic restrictions and impediments”; “to recognize and guarantee the ownership of property by individuals, either alone or in association with others”; “To solve the grave problem of massive unemployment”; “To ensure that the wealth of the country is not monopolized by a section or particular area of the country but is fairly shared and enjoyed by all”; “To protect the environment from degradation”; and “To ensure that there are equal opportunities for all citizens without discrimination on any grounds whether of gender, age, position, politics, religion or status”.

a3460.speaker: 2025 Budget Speech presented by Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, Minister of Finance, to the Parliament of Ghana
a3460.name: 2025 Budget Speech presented by Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson
a3460.title: Minister of Finance, to the Parliament of Ghana
a3460.speech: According to the 2025 Budget Speech, the sustainability and functionality of the 2025 Budget of Mahama's government is anchored on key policies of previous NPP governments: the Earmarked Funds Capping and Realignment Act, 2017 (Act 947), under which the NHIL, Road Fund and GNPC will receive full allocation (Section 135, Page 37); the amendment of the Mineral Income Investment Fund (MIIF) Act, 2018 (Act 978) so that 80% of mineral royalties are transferred to the Consolidated Fund for infrastructure development (Section 135, Page 37); an increase of the Growth & Sustainability Levy from 1% to 3% on the gross production of mining companies with the sunset clause extended to 2028 (Section 157, Pages 44-45); the extension of the sunset clause for the Special Import Levy to 2028 (Section 158, Page 45); and continued reforms and increased budgetary allocations for the four targeted social protection programmes — NHIS, LEAP, School Feeding Programme and Capitation Grant (Section 209, Page 61).

a3460.speaker: Razak Kojo Opoku (PhD), Lecturer/Founding President of UP Tradition Institute (issued statement)
a3460.name: Razak Kojo Opoku (PhD)
a3460.title: Lecturer/Founding President of UP Tradition Institute (issued statement)
