a3460.speech: Argued that the continuation of NPP's policy interventions under Mahama's government, such as Free SHS Policy, School Feeding Programme, Capitation Grant and payments of Teacher Trainee and Nursing Trainee Allowances, “clearly show that NPP is a strategic asset for the development of Ghana,” and that “the 120 days of Mahama's government has proven that, NPP government is still better managers of the Ghanaian economy especially in the midst of adversities” ; commended “President John Mahama for ensuring the continuation and sustainability of the aforementioned NPP Policies and Programmes including the Agenda 111 Hospitals,” stating that continuity of national projects by successive governments is one of the best approaches to accelerating national development in Ghana ; said that in 2028 the NPP “with the appropriate Presidential Candidate and Parliamentary Candidates coupled with Unity of Purpose would stand the greater chance of winning power from the NDC,” and that the legacies of Kufuor and Akufo-Addo are the party's “surest trump cards and unique selling proposition (USP) for 2028 general election.”

a3602.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a3602.name: William Ruto
a3602.title: President of Kenya
a3602.speech: In the wake of Trump's win, said his country “stands ready” to deepen its ties with Washington.

a3602.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a3602.name: Bola Tinubu
a3602.title: President of Nigeria
a3602.speech: spoke of a second Trump administration ushering in an era of “earnest, beneficial, and reciprocal” cooperation.

a3602.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a3602.name: Donald Trump
a3602.title: US President-elect
a3602.speech: once described African countries as “shithole countries.”

a3602.speaker: Charles Ray, chair of the Foreign Policy Research Institute’s Africa Program
a3602.name: Charles Ray
a3602.title: chair of the Foreign Policy Research Institute’s Africa Program
a3602.speech: said U.S. foreign policy has not made Africa a priority for a long while — beyond seeing the continent through the lens of countering rivals such as Russia and China. Africa “will be at the very bottom of (Trump's) list of priorities” and any U.S. action on the continent would likely be driven by his “transactional, ego-driven leadership style,” Ray added.

a3602.speaker: Charles Ray, chair of the Foreign Policy Research Institute’s Africa Program
a3602.name: Charles Ray
a3602.title: chair of the Foreign Policy Research Institute’s Africa Program
a3602.speech: said countries that undermine U.S. interests under trade programs “will be treated as pariahs.”

a3602.speaker: Murithi Mutiga, program director for Africa at the Crisis Group
a3602.name: Murithi Mutiga
a3602.title: program director for Africa at the Crisis Group
a3602.speech: says the president-elect is “a committed isolationist and clearly wants to pull back” on various fronts across the world.

a3602.speaker: Murithi Mutiga, program director for Africa at the Crisis Group
a3602.name: Murithi Mutiga
a3602.title: program director for Africa at the Crisis Group
a3602.speech: says “the problem historically has been that the U.S. and the West viewed Africa as a problem” to be solved. China and others “saw it as an opportunity to be grasped.” ; “The question is often, what will Washington do, but, really, what is Africa’s interest?” ; “We’re in an age of transactional global relations and unless Africa can engage in a way that articulates its own interests, America’s (interests in Africa) will continue to be determined by geopolitical competition with its rivals,” he said.

a3602.speaker: J. Peter Pham, Trump's former special envoy to Africa's Great Lakes and Sahel regions
a3602.name: J. Peter Pham
a3602.title: Trump's former special envoy to Africa's Great Lakes and Sahel regions
a3602.speech: says the next Trump presidency may look for a “win-win” situation in Africa. That could include a renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which grants eligible African countries duty-free access to U.S. markets, Pham said during a Voice of America broadcast. ; However, U.S. lawmakers have been asking questions about whether African countries are complying with conditions under the program — or if they are undermining U.S. foreign policy interests and national security, Pham said. ; Basically, you don't “kick America in the teeth” in ways that raise questions about compliance with such deals, Pham said.

a3602.speaker: Reuben Brigety, U.S. Ambassador [to South Africa]
a3602.name: Reuben Brigety
a3602.title: U.S. Ambassador [to South Africa]
a3602.speech: accused South Africa in 2023 of providing weapons and ammunition to Russia for its war in Ukraine and brought its professed neutral stance on the war into question.

a3602.speaker: Valentine Damitoni, a mother at 18 who visits a U.S.-funded clinic in Harare, Zimbabwe
a3602.name: Valentine Damitoni
a3602.title: a mother at 18 who visits a U.S.-funded clinic in Harare, Zimbabwe
a3602.speech: “The situation is already bad for girls (and) it will turn into a disaster without these services,” she said.

a3602.speaker: Max Primorac, former acting deputy administrator of USAID (in Project 2025, Heritage Foundation blueprint)
a3602.name: Max Primorac
a3602.title: former acting deputy administrator of USAID (in Project 2025, Heritage Foundation blueprint)
a3602.speech: criticized some of the agency's programs in Project 2025, a 900-page blueprint proposed by the conservative-leaning Heritage Foundation to reshape the federal government. In particular, Primorac criticized USAID programs that “promote abortion, climate extremism and interventions against perceived systematic racism.”

a3602.speaker: Kiron Skinner, head of policy planning at the U.S. State Department during Trump’s first term (in Project 2025 document)
a3602.name: Kiron Skinner
a3602.title: head of policy planning at the U.S. State Department during Trump’s first term (in Project 2025 document)
a3602.speech: recommends in the document that in Africa, America should “focus on core security, economic, and human rights” rather than impose “radical abortion and pro-LGBT initiatives.”

a3602.speaker: Biden administration
a3602.name: Biden administration
a3602.speech: announced last December that it had invested at least $22 billion in Africa and promised to do more.

a3602.speaker: Isah Mohammed, a fruit seller in Nigeria's capital, Abuja
a3602.name: Isah Mohammed
a3602.title: a fruit seller in Nigeria's capital, Abuja
a3602.speech: “Trump ... is not going to save us from hunger caused by our government,” he said.

a3602.speaker: Assabah newspaper (Morocco), editorial
a3602.name: Assabah newspaper (Morocco)
a3602.title: editorial
a3602.speech: “The return of the friend of Morocco to the White House,” proclaimed the country's Assabah newspaper in its editorial.

a3602.speaker: Rashid Abdi, analyst at the Nairobi-based Sahan Research think tank
a3602.name: Rashid Abdi
a3602.title: analyst at the Nairobi-based Sahan Research think tank
a3602.speech: predicts Trump will likely cut funding to Somalia and engage more with Somaliland.

a3602.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a3602.name: Joe Biden
a3602.title: US President
a3602.speech: had said the African Union’s admission to the G20 as a permanent member was “a long time in coming.”

a3640.speaker: Margaret Mensah-Williams, Namibia's Ambassador to the United States and Canada
a3640.name: Margaret Mensah-Williams
a3640.title: Namibia's Ambassador to the United States and Canada
a3640.speech: Has expressed condolences to the families of three Namibians who died in the U.S. and Canada over the past two weeks ; announced the deaths of health workers Nelson Kondjayi Dumeni, who suffered a heart failure in Washington, DC, on December 21, and Wesley Katimba, who died on New Year's Day ; says Katimba was returning from church an hour after midnight when he was hit by a car in Montreal, Canada.

a3669.speaker: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene, Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.name: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene
a3669.title: Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.speech: "Consuming local means supporting our economy, honoring our heritage, and expressing our attachment to the nation."

a3669.speaker: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene, Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.name: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene
a3669.title: Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.speech: Delivered a message in which she recalled the importance of the National Handicrafts Day, an unmissable appointment to give value to a sector that constitutes the economic and cultural soul of the country ; underlined the objectives assigned to this day, instituted in 2017 as part of the National Policy for the Development of Handicrafts (PNDA) adopted in 1992: increasing the visibility of Nigerien artisanal know-how nationally and internationally, promoting local consumption as a true patriotic act and lever of economic empowerment, and improving the living and working conditions of artisans.

a3669.speaker: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene, Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.name: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene
a3669.title: Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.speech: Underlined that in a context marked by economic, security and social challenges, handicrafts stand out as a bulwark against precariousness, a sector deeply rooted in Nigerien traditions but resolutely turned toward the future, capable of generating thousands of sustainable jobs, particularly for young people and women, now covering more than 291 trade bodies.

a3669.speaker: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene, Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.name: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene
a3669.title: Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.speech: Maintained that the carefully chosen theme reflects the government's will to show how much handicrafts are at the heart of economic sovereignty: by relying on local resources and human capital, Niger reduces its dependence on imports, creates wealth inside the country, and strengthens resilience in the face of crises ; said this edition is being held in an encouraging context, marked by a growing mobilization of artisans to give value to local distribution circuits and to use national raw materials such as cowpea, moringa, maize, leather and local stones.

a3669.speaker: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene, Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.name: Soufiane Aghaichata Guichene
a3669.title: Nigerien Minister of Handicrafts and Tourism
a3669.speech: Indicated that the country's highest authorities have reaffirmed their determination to support the handicrafts sector within the framework of the National Refoundation Program, through strengthening the competitiveness of Nigerien artisanal products, simplifying tourist reception and stay procedures, promoting domestic tourism, and establishing a rigorous framework for evaluating the Ministry's performance ; invited all Nigeriens to participate massively in the exhibition-sales in the artisanal villages throughout the regions in order to admire the talent, ingenuity and courage of the artisans and to buy their products.

a3687.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.name: Li Jian
a3687.title: Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.speech: In a speech delivered live on Facebook on Wednesday 26 May 2021, on the occasion of the third anniversary of the restoration of Sino-Burkinabè relations, argued for the deepening of cooperation between the two countries: “It is a great pleasure to meet you on the occasion of the third anniversary of the restoration of diplomatic relations between the Republic of China and Burkina Faso. Three years ago, to the day, the Chinese State Councillor and Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Mr WANG Yi and his Burkinabè counterpart H.E. Mr Alpha BARRY signed the joint communiqué marking the resumption of Sino-Burkinabè diplomatic relations. Since then, that date has been inscribed and engraved in the history of Sino-African relations.” ; “I have now been living and working in Burkina Faso for three years. Here, it is like a great construction site where everything is moving forward step by step... I am delighted and at the same time galvanised by the wisdom, tolerance, perseverance and dynamism of Burkina Faso, advancing along its own path of development, and by the patriotism, bravery, diligence and optimism of the Burkinabè people.”

a3687.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.name: Li Jian
a3687.title: Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.speech: On the results of Sino-Burkinabè cooperation: said cooperation has yielded fruitful results in health, education, agriculture and infrastructure, that the 113 school complexes financed by China have been fully completed, that the Chinese side is coordinating the final technical aspects of the Bobo-Dioulasso hospital project, that 5,331 tonnes of rice in emergency food aid will shortly be handed over in full, and that the “Smart Burkina” project is expected to start very soon ; “Rest assured that on Burkina Faso’s path of socio-economic development, China will never fail to be present and to provide its support accordingly.” ; said Chinese technical cooperation missions (medical, agricultural, vocational training and the millet project) have worked hard down to distant villages and fields, and that under the “Brightness Action” some twenty Chinese ophthalmologists from a hospital in Wenzhou performed free cataract operations on more than 400 Burkinabè in 2018 and 2019 with a 100% success rate ; said that in 2020 China launched a mechanism exempting customs duties on 97% of Burkinabè products exported to China and that trade volume reached 400 million dollars in 2020, up 24.5% on the previous year, a new record.

a3687.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.name: Li Jian
a3687.title: Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.speech: On Covid-19 cooperation: said that as soon as the first confirmed case was notified in Burkina Faso, China mobilised on a large scale, bringing in by special flights more than a million masks, some ten thousand protective suits, some twenty thousand PCR reagent tests and about a hundred ventilators and oxygen machines; that China financed the rehabilitation of two isolation buildings at the Yalgado Ouédraogo University Hospital and the emergency department of the Koudougou Regional Hospital; and that in April 2020 the Chinese government sent a team of doctors specialised in fighting Covid-19 ; “We must therefore continue to remain vigilant and united, to deepen our cooperation in the field of health and to constantly improve our capacities in human resources, infrastructure and equipment in order always to be able to meet long-term challenges.”

a3687.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.name: Li Jian
a3687.title: Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.speech: On China’s development model and poverty reduction: said this year marks the centenary of the founding of the Chinese Communist Party, which is leading 1.4 billion Chinese and in 100 years has built a moderately prosperous society enabling 800 million Chinese to emerge definitively from absolute poverty ; “China has succeeded in finding its own path of development, and the development miracle in China shows the whole world, especially developing countries and African countries, that it is entirely possible for a country, previously oppressed and underdeveloped, to rise again with sovereignty, dignity, independence and the satisfaction of its people.” ; “China has the will, the experience and the capacity to help Burkina Faso achieve this objective and win victory over poverty” ; said more than 800 professionals have travelled to China for training or seminars, about a hundred Burkinabè students have received Chinese scholarships, and more than 20 online seminars are planned this year for 500 professionals.

a3687.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.name: Li Jian
a3687.title: Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
a3687.speech: Called on the international community to increase its investments and support for Africa in general and Burkina Faso in particular: “Efforts must converge towards Burkina Faso to help the country recover as soon as possible from the negative effects of the Covid-19 pandemic and to return to its momentum of growth” ; expressed his sincere thanks to all those who support the development of Sino-Burkinabè relations, and said: “I am firmly convinced that, with the continued deepening of Sino-Burkinabè cooperation, we will open a golden period of the new era for the development of our two countries and for the happiness of our two peoples.”

a3687.speaker: Adama Compaoré, Ambassador of Burkina Faso to China
a3687.name: Adama Compaoré
a3687.title: Ambassador of Burkina Faso to China
a3687.speech: Noted in an interview that China has played an important and constructive role in the economic and social development process of Burkina Faso.

a3687.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese State Councillor and Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3687.name: Wang Yi
a3687.title: Chinese State Councillor and Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3687.speech: Affirmed in a full session of the UN Security Council, during the Chinese presidency in May, that as a brother, friend and partner China will always defend the interests of African countries and will not hesitate to undertake all useful actions for the benefit of African peoples ; at the celebration of Africa Day, reaffirmed that strengthening unity and cooperation with African countries constitutes the constant priority of Chinese diplomacy.

a3687.speaker: Christophe Joseph Marie Dabiré, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a3687.name: Christophe Joseph Marie Dabiré
a3687.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a3687.speech: Stressed in his State of the Nation Address that one of the main objectives of the Burkinabè government for the next five years is the reduction of poverty.

a3891.speaker: Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS), co-manager of the Niassa Special Reserve
a3891.name: Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS)
a3891.title: co-manager of the Niassa Special Reserve
a3891.speech: Announced on Friday that the Niassa Special Reserve (REN), the largest in Mozambique, needs $8.4 million (EUR 7.7 million) annually for management and maintenance. ; According to WCS data, it is estimated that the Niassa National Reserve represents 21% of Mozambique's Protected Areas Network and 51% of its parks and land reserves, making it "part of an elite and increasingly rare group of only seven protected 'mega-areas'" in sub-Saharan Africa. ; According to WCS, the main challenges in the Niassa National Reserve are the need to increase and train the number of inspectors, increase aerial surveillance, increase the means to enable a more reactive, proactive and efficient monitoring and inspection capacity and establish more partnerships to cover the costs of training and the acquisition of means to mitigate human-wildlife conflict and community work.

a3891.speaker: Afonso Madopo, director of WCS
a3891.name: Afonso Madopo
a3891.title: director of WCS
a3891.speech: "This indicator reflects that we are still far below the 50% of needs," said Afonso Madopo during the celebration of the 70th anniversary of the creation of the REN. ; "These investments have been crucial not only for biodiversity conservation but also for the socio-economic development of the communities," said Afonso Madopo.

a3891.speaker: Ministry of Land and Environment (information released on the 70th anniversary)
a3891.name: Ministry of Land and Environment (information released on the 70th anniversary)
a3891.speech: Investments and legal reforms over the last ten years "have brought new dynamics and huge gains to conservation areas, particularly the Niassa Special Reserve". ; "The reduction in illegal activities, with the highlight being the zero deaths of elephants by poachers as of 2019 and for three consecutive years, and the growing increase in fauna in the order of 10% to 27% are some of the greatest achievements of the government and the reserve's administration in particular," the information adds.

a3891.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a3891.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a3891.speech: Also at the REN anniversary ceremony, USAID, which has funded various environmental programmes in the area, said it will continue to do so in the coming years.

a3891.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID's director in Mozambique
a3891.name: Helen Pataki
a3891.title: USAID's director in Mozambique
a3891.speech: "We will continue to support initiatives that conserve wildlife and empower communities to protect their natural resources," said Helen Pataki.

a3945.speaker: Ghanaian Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness & Industry (press release)
a3945.name: Ghanaian Ministry of Trade
a3945.title: Agribusiness & Industry (press release)
a3945.speech: Announced plans to urgently engage the United States over the newly imposed 10 per cent universal tariff and assured exporters and investors of its commitment to resolving the issue to avoid trade disruptions: “The Ministry as a matter of urgency, is also engaging relevant stakeholders to determine the extent of the effect and assess the full impact of the US tariffs on the country’s economy” ; emphasized its dedication to keeping the private sector informed, stating, “The Government is committed to ensuring that the private sector is well informed on the details of the imposition to avoid trade disruption as well as ensure predictability of investment decisions in the country.”

a3945.speaker: United States government (tariff announcement of 2 April 2025 under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977)
a3945.name: United States government (tariff announcement of 2 April 2025 under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977)
a3945.speech: Cites economic and national security concerns linked to global trade deficits, with certain products – such as copper, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and critical minerals – exempt from the 10 per cent levy.

a4065.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4065.name: Donald Trump
a4065.title: US President
a4065.speech: Claimed there was a project of "eight million dollars to promote LGBTQI+ in the African nation of Lesotho" during an address to Congress defending his sweeping cuts in aid, calling Lesotho a country "Which nobody has ever heard of," as Republican lawmakers laughed.

a4065.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Foreign Minister of Lesotho
a4065.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a4065.title: Foreign Minister of Lesotho
a4065.speech: Told AFP the Lesotho government was "shocked and embarrassed" by the comments ; "We did not expect a head of state to refer to another sovereign nation in such a manner" ; "We are not taking this matter lightly," adding that they will send an official protest letter to Washington.

a4065.speaker: Tampose Mothopeng, spokesperson for the People's Matrix (Lesotho's main LGBTQ rights organisation)
a4065.name: Tampose Mothopeng
a4065.title: spokesperson for the People's Matrix (Lesotho's main LGBTQ rights organisation)
a4065.speech: Denied receiving eight million dollars in US funding: "We are literally not receiving grants from the US" ; "We do not know who received or is going to receive that money" ; "We do not have such moneys or a contract that would even reach a quarter of half of that money."

a4065.speaker: US government foreign assistance website
a4065.name: US government foreign assistance website
a4065.speech: Did not list any financial support for LGBTQ rights in Lesotho; instead it indicated that about 120 million dollars had been spent on "health and population" programmes in the country in 2024, including $43.5 million to tackle HIV/AIDS.

a4065.speaker: US embassy in Lesotho
a4065.name: US embassy in Lesotho
a4065.speech: According to it, the US has committed more than $630 million since 2006 to anti-HIV/AIDS efforts in Lesotho.

a4065.speaker: More than 30 non-governmental organisations
a4065.name: More than 30 non-governmental organisations
a4065.speech: Warned in mid-February that the country's HIV programmes were at risk of collapse following the loss of US foreign aid.

a4065.speaker: Kananelo Boloetse, journalist and activist
a4065.name: Kananelo Boloetse
a4065.title: journalist and activist
a4065.speech: Posted on social media platform X: "Ever heard of Kingdom in the Sky? Guess not, too busy golfing to notice" ; "Lesotho's the only country in the world entirely above 1 000 metres elevation, higher than your approval ratings ever got" ; "We're here, we're proud, and we're not your punchline."

a4072.speaker: An Ethiopian official (unnamed)
a4072.name: An Ethiopian official (unnamed)
a4072.speech: Disclosed on Wednesday that tens of thousands of pastoralists residing in the Awash Fentale district, near the Kesem Dam in the Afar region of Ethiopia, are being relocated to evacuation centers following increasing volcanic activity across the Ethiopian Rift Valley.

a4072.speaker: Government of Ethiopia
a4072.name: Government of Ethiopia
a4072.speech: Announced over the weekend the relocation of 80,000 residents to other places.

a4072.speaker: United States Geological Survey (USGS)
a4072.name: United States Geological Survey (USGS)
a4072.speech: Recorded last Saturday the largest earthquake, measuring a magnitude of 5.8, about 56 kilometers (35 miles) southeast of Ambosa, in the Oromia region, in the early hours of Saturday.

a4072.speaker: Atalay Ayele, head of the Seismology Department and professor of seismic science at Addis Ababa University
a4072.name: Atalay Ayele
a4072.title: head of the Seismology Department and professor of seismic science at Addis Ababa University
a4072.speech: Says the epicenter was in the middle of Dofen Mountain, Awash Fentale district, in the Afar region.

a4072.speaker: Ahmed Ibrahim, the zone's command post coordinator
a4072.name: Ahmed Ibrahim
a4072.title: the zone's command post coordinator
a4072.speech: Confirming the relocation of pastoralists, stated that humanitarian assistance is being provided to those affected by the relocation process.

a4072.speaker: Binyam Wubshat, representative of the Kesem Dam administration
a4072.name: Binyam Wubshat
a4072.title: representative of the Kesem Dam administration
a4072.speech: “The Kesem Dam, constructed to mitigate land erosion, is designed to withstand earthquakes up to a magnitude of seven on the Richter scale” ; “No issues related to land displacement have been reported thus far.”

a4072.speaker: Government of Ethiopia (statement)
a4072.name: Government of Ethiopia (statement)
a4072.speech: “The government is closely monitoring the events with experts in the field. In addition, it has identified the epicenter of the earthquake and deployed emergency workers from various fields in 12 localities to assess the extent of the damage.”

a4345.speaker: Guillaume Aguettant, Country Director of Care Benin/Togo
a4345.name: Guillaume Aguettant
a4345.title: Country Director of Care Benin/Togo
a4345.speech: Indicated that since the signing of the headquarters agreement on 9 September 1999 in Benin, Care has played a crucial role in improving communities' living conditions and strengthening the capacities of local partners ; welcomed that in twenty-five years of existence Care Benin has established itself as a key development actor, operating in all 77 communes of the country with a strong concentration in the four northern departments ; indicated that in 2023 the organisation was able to reach nearly 500,000 people through 21 development projects and two humanitarian projects, with a total budget of 14.37 million dollars, or 8.69 billion CFA francs.

a4345.speaker: Claudine Awute Mensah, Vice-President for Programs and Operations of Care International, former Country Director of Care Benin/Togo
a4345.name: Claudine Awute Mensah
a4345.title: Vice-President for Programs and Operations of Care International, former Country Director of Care Benin/Togo
a4345.speech: Praised that the organisation stands out for its dynamic and committed staff, with a strong representation of young people under 35, and constitutes a family where talents emerge and flourish in the service of communities.

a4345.speaker: Balla Sidibe, Care Regional Director for West Africa
a4345.name: Balla Sidibe
a4345.title: Care Regional Director for West Africa
a4345.speech: Stressed that Care has managed to build a solid and diversified network of partners, including international institutions such as USAID, the World Bank, the European Union, the Kingdom of the Netherlands, Swiss Cooperation, as well as members of Care International such as Care USA, Care France, Care Luxembourg and Care Canada, to name only those ; indicated that this diversity of partnerships allows the organisation to carry out multisectoral projects responding to the needs of the most vulnerable populations.

a4345.speaker: Alain Troukou, Director of Program Quality and Resource Mobilisation (Care Benin)
a4345.name: Alain Troukou
a4345.title: Director of Program Quality and Resource Mobilisation (Care Benin)
a4345.speech: Assured that Care Benin reaffirms its commitment to continue its work in four priority areas: economic and gender justice, maternal, child and youth health, food and nutrition security, and emergency preparedness and response ; continued that with the ambition of reaching 2.8 million people by 2026, the organisation looks to the future with the will to contribute to defeating poverty and social injustice.

a4612.speaker: Dr Mutumwa Muyangana, medical officer, Centre for Infectious Disease Research in Zambia (CIDRZ) / USAID-TBLON
a4612.name: Dr Mutumwa Muyangana
a4612.title: medical officer, Centre for Infectious Disease Research in Zambia (CIDRZ) / USAID-TBLON
a4612.speech: “These concentrators will enable the hospitals to provide critical care treatment to not only TB patients but also other patients who may require oxygen support.”

a4612.speaker: Dr Musaku Mwenechanya, senior medical superintendent, UTH Children's Hospital
a4612.name: Dr Musaku Mwenechanya
a4612.title: senior medical superintendent, UTH Children's Hospital
a4612.speech: Said the donation is welcome as the institution spends huge amounts of money to procure oxygen concentrators. “We have pneumonia children who need oxygen.” ; “The hospital spends a lot of money to procure oxygen concentrators and this helps reduce the expenditure burden on the hospital.”

a4631.speaker: Madalitso Ziwaoh, Balaka-based visual artist
a4631.name: Madalitso Ziwaoh
a4631.title: Balaka-based visual artist
a4631.speech: Said art is powerful and that it plays a huge role in preserving history. "I have created several artworks of the country's heroes and John Chilembwe is there. The freedom we are enjoying today is because of these heroes, they fought for it. Looking back, I am reminded that we must respect those who fought for our freedom."

a4631.speaker: Rhoda Zulu, writer
a4631.name: Rhoda Zulu
a4631.title: writer
a4631.speech: In her verses, Zulu asks thought-provoking questions as to whether the freedom that Chilembwe and others fought for is there today. "I wrote these poems to remind Malawians that the freedom we are enjoying today was not free. We must honour those who fought for our freedom and continue working towards a brighter future for our nation."

a4786.speaker: Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) / report on Benin's balance of payments for 2020
a4786.name: Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) / report on Benin's balance of payments for 2020
a4786.speech: Recommends strengthening the promotion and production of goods and services that substitute for imports in the WAEMU and, specifically for Benin, pursuing efforts to diversify the economy ; "These measures could in particular concern the lifting of the constraints that hamper the dynamism and competitiveness of the Union's private sector, notably through policies favouring the reduction of factor costs and support for exports; the deepening of structural reforms, through the consolidation of common sectoral policies in the areas of transport and tourism as well as the continued restructuring of agricultural value chains; the strengthening of infrastructure (transport, energy, telecommunications, finance)" ; at the national level recommends diversifying the economy through identified agricultural value chains, strengthening trade relations with Nigeria, keeping the business climate attractive and using Public-Private Partnerships, strengthening the energy supply in line with the second Millennium Challenge Account compact, consolidating the mobilisation of domestic resources, and preserving the sustainability of public debt.

a4786.speaker: Report on Benin's balance of payments for 2020 (conclusions)
a4786.name: Report on Benin's balance of payments for 2020 (conclusions)
a4786.speech: Indicate that efforts are being made in public finances in Benin; the overall balance of payments shows a surplus of 306,937.9 million CFA francs in 2020, following the surplus (45,550.6 million) of 2019, and the overall external position shows a net financial liability of 2,974,227.7 million as at 31 December 2020 against 2,974,804.5 million as at 31 December 2019.

a4799.speaker: Lagos State Coconut Development Authority (LASCODA)
a4799.name: Lagos State Coconut Development Authority (LASCODA)
a4799.speech: According to it, Nigeria currently produces between 265,000 and 300,000 metric tonnes of coconut annually, accounting for barely 25 per cent of the country’s growing domestic demand.

a4799.speaker: John Oladapo Olakulehin, former general manager of LASCODA
a4799.name: John Oladapo Olakulehin
a4799.title: former general manager of LASCODA
a4799.speech: In an interview highlighted a critical three-tiered problem within the sector’s production, processing and marketing process. “Our coconut demand is exploding, but domestic production is stagnant. We are importing what we should be exporting. Seventy per cent of coconuts consumed in Nigeria are sourced from Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire, The Gambia and Philippines. These import trends cost Nigeria billions of naira annually.”

a4799.speaker: Dr Chinelo Obasi, agricultural economist
a4799.name: Dr Chinelo Obasi
a4799.title: agricultural economist
a4799.speech: Explained that Nigeria’s coconut value chain had the potential to generate over N500 billion annually if properly structured. “This includes upstream farming, midstream processing and downstream export. But the sector remains largely informal, under-capitalised and fragmented.”

a4799.speaker: Chief Bassey Etim, coconut farmer in Akwa Ibom
a4799.name: Chief Bassey Etim
a4799.title: coconut farmer in Akwa Ibom
a4799.speech: “We don’t have access to improved seedlings, fertilisers or irrigation. Sometimes our coconuts rot because there’s no processing plant nearby. Buyers dictate the prices. We are farming gold but selling it like firewood.”

a4799.speaker: Ben Odion, Lagos-based food scientist
a4799.name: Ben Odion
a4799.title: Lagos-based food scientist
a4799.speech: Expressed concern over the growing sale of fake coconut oil in Nigerian markets. “Because of high demand, some producers mix coconut oil with paraffin, palm kernel oil or chemical thickeners to increase volume and profits. This not only puts consumers at risk but also damages the credibility of genuine local producers.” ; “Without regulatory oversight and enforcement, we risk flooding the market with fake products that threaten lives and livelihoods.”

a4799.speaker: Current general manager of LASCODA, and the president of NACOPMANN (non-response)
a4799.name: Current general manager of LASCODA
a4799.title: and the president of NACOPMANN (non-response)
a4799.speech: The current general manager of LASCODA failed to provide any formal update, and multiple attempts to contact the president of NACOPMANN also proved abortive. Calls, emails and official messages went unanswered at the time of filing this report.

a5018.speaker: Charity Gladstone, MBE, president of the Malawian-UK Nurses Association (MUNA) (report on the Summit)
a5018.name: Charity Gladstone
a5018.title: MBE, president of the Malawian-UK Nurses Association (MUNA) (report on the Summit)
a5018.speech: Said that, under the theme of ‘Leaving No One Behind’, the Summit highlighted the importance of ensuring equal access to healthcare for all individuals worldwide, and that it brought together leaders, health professionals and global health advocates to share solutions for health for all; indicated that Health Minister Kandodo Chiponda shared “valuable insights and perspectives on the importance of global health equity and challenges Malawi face”; reported that the MUNA delegation “made many connections in terms of NGOs and UK-based voluntary organisations making an impact in Malawi” ; “Overall, the Summit was enlightening and it was a privilege for MUNA to be invited to such an important event. I believe that the knowledge and experiences we gained will greatly benefit our own projects and initiatives.”

a5018.speaker: Charity Gladstone, MBE, president of MUNA (report on the Minister’s address)
a5018.name: Charity Gladstone
a5018.title: MBE, president of MUNA (report on the Minister’s address)
a5018.speech: The report adds that the Minister of Health delivered “a compelling keynote address, underscoring the indispensable role of diaspora professionals in bridging health inequalities between the UK and Africa”: “She did not shy away from the pressing challenges of our time — she called them by name and with urgency and conviction, she highlighted the deepening workforce crisis, where overstretched and under-resourced health systems are struggling to meet the growing demands of care.”

a5018.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Malawi Minister of Health
a5018.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a5018.title: Malawi Minister of Health
a5018.speech: “The burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) — silent killers such as hypertension, diabetes, and cancer that continue to devastate communities — yet remain overshadowed by more immediate crises. Climate change is a warning that it is not just an environmental issue, but a health catastrophe that disproportionately affects the most vulnerable. We cannot afford to treat these as separate challenges — they are intertwined. And they demand a unified, urgent response. Health systems must be resilient, responsive, and inclusive. And the diaspora — our bridge between nations — must be at the heart of that transformation.”

a5018.speaker: Dr. Martin Luther King Jnr (quoted by Charity Gladstone)
a5018.name: Dr. Martin Luther King Jnr (quoted by Charity Gladstone)
a5018.speech: “Of all the forms of inequality, injustice in health is the most shocking and inhuman.”

a5018.speaker: Charity Gladstone, MBE, president of MUNA (speech on ‘Leaving No One Behind’)
a5018.name: Charity Gladstone
a5018.title: MBE, president of MUNA (speech on ‘Leaving No One Behind’)
a5018.speech: Emphasised that healthcare should be a fundamental right, not a privilege dictated by race, wealth, or geography, and reinforced the responsibility of the diaspora in shaping a just and equitable world: “The world we dream of — one of equity, dignity, and justice — will not be handed to us. We must rise, we must build, and we must claim our place in shaping it. Change is not a gift — it is a fight, a commitment, and a legacy we create for those who come after us.” ; stressed that the Summit came to a close with a clear message: “diaspora professionals must not only be seen but must be integrated as equal partners in shaping global health” ; “As MUNA’s delegation returned from the Summit, their call to action echoed beyond the conference halls. The future will not be given — we must build it. The principle of Ubuntu (‘I am because we are’) reminds us that true progress is collective. The question is not whether diaspora professionals belong at the table — the real question is: Can global health afford to exclude them?”

a5018.speaker: Charity Gladstone, MBE, president of MUNA (on CoVID-19 and inequality)
a5018.name: Charity Gladstone
a5018.title: MBE, president of MUNA (on CoVID-19 and inequality)
a5018.speech: Reflecting on the CoVID-19 pandemic, reminded the audience that the crisis laid bare the structural inequalities in global health: “While public health restrictions affected everyone, the burden was not shared equally”; highlighted how CoVID-19 magnified pre-existing disparities — the global divide, where high-income countries had better resources and faster recovery while lower-income nations struggled for essential supplies, and where the recent cuts in foreign aid threaten to further disadvantage those living with both communicable and non-communicable diseases, including HIV/Aids; mistrust in the system rooted in historical injustices; language and cultural barriers; limited healthcare access for undocumented migrants and marginalized groups in the UK; and power imbalance, with diaspora professionals often excluded from mainstream policy discussions due to the lack of a formal diaspora health policy.

a5018.speaker: Patrick Vundule, speaking on behalf of MUNA
a5018.name: Patrick Vundule
a5018.title: speaking on behalf of MUNA
a5018.speech: Expressed deep gratitude for the sponsorship and support provided by Global Health Partnerships (formerly THET): “The work we do as diaspora professionals is strengthened by the partnerships that believe in our mission. Global Health Partnerships has played a crucial role in amplifying our voices and enabling us to make a tangible impact. This kind of collaboration is essential if we are to truly leave no one behind.”

a5018.speaker: Charity Gladstone, MBE, president of MUNA (on her MBE award)
a5018.name: Charity Gladstone
a5018.title: MBE, president of MUNA (on her MBE award)
a5018.speech: Upon receiving the honour, said modestly that the MBE is an overall recognition of the charity work that MUNA does, both in the UK and Malawi — with a passionate desire to support and empower one another and to raise and develop health standards in both countries.

a5034.speaker: Harriet Thompson, British High Commissioner to Ghana
a5034.name: Harriet Thompson
a5034.title: British High Commissioner to Ghana
a5034.speech: Has said the United Kingdom is proud to partner Ghana in advancing sustainable agriculture and climate resilience through the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra)-Animal Health System Strengthening (AHSS) Project in the country ; said the initiative was not only protecting pollinators and biodiversity but also empowering women, youth and academic institutions to lead the way in innovation and inclusive development ; “On World Bee Day, we celebrate the power of collaboration to create lasting impact.”

a5034.speaker: Professor Benjamin Emikpe, Dean of the School of Veterinary Medicine at KNUST
a5034.name: Professor Benjamin Emikpe
a5034.title: Dean of the School of Veterinary Medicine at KNUST
a5034.speech: “The AHSS Project has been a game-changer for Ghana’s honeybee sector. It has strengthened our veterinary education, created new economic opportunities for rural communities, and positioned Ghana as a leader in climate-smart beekeeping. We are grateful for the UK’s support and look forward to deepening this partnership for the benefit of our people and environment.”

a5034.speaker: UK High Commission (statement)
a5034.name: UK High Commission (statement)
a5034.speech: The statement said the AHSS Project was empowering Ghana’s institutions, women, and academic communities through climate-smart beekeeping, inclusive enterprise and modern veterinary education.

a5167.speaker: Barrick Gold (statement dated Wednesday 18 December 2024)
a5167.name: Barrick Gold (statement dated Wednesday 18 December 2024)
a5167.speech: Announced that it had requested arbitration by the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes to “settle the disagreements” with the government of Mali. “Barrick is seeking a fair solution in Mali through arbitration” ; confirms that its two operating companies in Mali, Loulo SA and Gounkoto SA, submitted a request for arbitration to ICSID in order “to comply with the stipulations of their respective Establishment Conventions with the State of Mali, to address the disagreements concerning the Loulo-Gounkoto complex” ; stresses that this step reflects its commitment to respecting established procedures for resolving disputes fairly and transparently ; “The arbitration mechanism, provided for by the Establishment Conventions of Somilo and Gounkoto concluded with the State, has proven in the past to be an effective tool for strengthening partnerships and finding mutually acceptable solutions through an independent and competent authority.”

a5167.speaker: Mark Bristow, President and Chief Executive Officer of Barrick Gold
a5167.name: Mark Bristow
a5167.title: President and Chief Executive Officer of Barrick Gold
a5167.speech: Recalls that his company has always demonstrated its long-term commitment to the country and its people over its three decades of activity in Mali. “Throughout this process, Barrick remains open to continued dialogue with the Government to resolve these issues amicably and ensure the long-term success of the Loulo-Gounkoto complex,” Mark Bristow insisted.

a5167.speaker: Barrick Gold
a5167.name: Barrick Gold
a5167.speech: Announced on Monday 16 December that the Malian government had blocked gold exports from Loulo-Gounkoto, specifying that maintaining this blockage could force it to “suspend its operations.”

a5167.speaker: Malian State (no confirmation or denial)
a5167.name: Malian State (no confirmation or denial)
a5167.speech: The blocking of gold exports from the country’s largest gold mine has been neither confirmed nor denied by the Malian State.

a5167.speaker: Malian justice system (court/judicial record)
a5167.name: Malian justice system (court/judicial record)
a5167.speech: A few days ago issued an arrest warrant against the chief executive officer of Barrick Gold; four senior Malian-national officials of the mine have been charged and detained on grounds of various financial misconduct.

a5167.speaker: Barrick Gold
a5167.name: Barrick Gold
a5167.speech: Has rejected the accusations of financial misconduct.

a5311.speaker: International Labour Organization (ILO) and UNICEF (joint report, "More than a billion reasons: the urgent need to build universal social protection for children")
a5311.name: International Labour Organization (ILO) and UNICEF (joint report
a5311.title: "More than a billion reasons: the urgent need to build universal social protection for children")
a5311.speech: According to the report, the multiplication of crises will push a greater number of children into poverty, hence the urgency of achieving progress in social protection; the region showing the weakest progress is Africa; 1.46 billion children under 15 are affected worldwide, with inevitable negative long-term repercussions on communities, societies and economies. The report states that social protection is a universal human right and an essential foundation for helping the world's most vulnerable children realise their potential, that 2.4 billion children need adequate social protection, that children are twice as likely as adults to live in poverty, that more than 800 million children live on less than $3.20 a day and 1.3 billion on less than $5.50 a day, that more than a billion children live in multidimensional poverty, that 1.5 billion children under 15 are deprived of access to social protection, and that progress towards increasing effective coverage globally has stagnated since 2016; it reports that coverage fell from 63.8% to 57.4% in the Americas, stands at 15.4% in the Arab States, fell from 84.6% to 82.3% in Europe and Central Asia, went from 12.8% to 12.6% in Africa (the lowest), and stands at about 18% in Asia and the Pacific.

a5311.speaker: International Labour Organization (ILO) and UNICEF
a5311.name: International Labour Organization (ILO) and UNICEF
a5311.speech: Said it is essential to improve the responsiveness of social protection systems to shocks in order to safeguard children's rights and put an end to the acceleration of child poverty triggered by crises, noting that children account for 41% of the 83.9 million people forcibly displaced worldwide, and that strengthening social protection systems and developing emerging systems on the foundations created by humanitarian aid could be part of the solution.

a5393.speaker: Dr. Efison Dhodho, Knowledge Manager, Zimbabwe College of Public Health Physicians and Director of Strategic Information at OPHID
a5393.name: Dr. Efison Dhodho
a5393.title: Knowledge Manager, Zimbabwe College of Public Health Physicians and Director of Strategic Information at OPHID
a5393.speech: on what drove him into medicine: “There was no doctor in Mwenezi at that time because there was no hospital. But seeing the work my mother and other nurses did, ignited a desire to say I want to make a difference here,” he said in an interview.

a5393.speaker: Dr. Efison Dhodho, Knowledge Manager, Zimbabwe College of Public Health Physicians and Director of Strategic Information at OPHID
a5393.name: Dr. Efison Dhodho
a5393.title: Knowledge Manager, Zimbabwe College of Public Health Physicians and Director of Strategic Information at OPHID
a5393.speech: on his housemanship: “I was deployed to Bulawayo for my housemanship. This sent me to Mpilo Hospital, which catered to rural Matabeleland. On one hand, I was happy that I was going to serve the rural people as was always my wish, on the other hand, I did not know the language.”

a5393.speaker: Dr. Efison Dhodho, Knowledge Manager, Zimbabwe College of Public Health Physicians and Director of Strategic Information at OPHID
a5393.name: Dr. Efison Dhodho
a5393.title: Knowledge Manager, Zimbabwe College of Public Health Physicians and Director of Strategic Information at OPHID
a5393.speech: highlighted that at the time, Binga had 11 clinics for a population of 140 000 and the furthest clinic was 230 km from the hospital: “Every clinic was not reachable, there was no network and for one to call using a cell phone, he/she needed to get a Zambian line. So we used to communicate using the Save the Children radios. This was a low resource setting and that is when I began to learn to innovate, push boundaries, and think outside the box to succeed in such areas.”

a5393.speaker: Dr. Efison Dhodho, Knowledge Manager, Zimbabwe College of Public Health Physicians and Director of Strategic Information at OPHID
a5393.name: Dr. Efison Dhodho
a5393.title: Knowledge Manager, Zimbabwe College of Public Health Physicians and Director of Strategic Information at OPHID
a5393.speech: on decentralising ART delivery in Binga: “With my team, I decided to engage the community. I met with chiefs because HIV carried a lot of stigma. I told them, ‘We’re going to distribute ARVs in an unconventional way. But first, I need your support. To lead by example, I want you to be tested for HIV, and I’ll personally conduct the tests. The results will remain confidential.’ The chiefs agreed, and they were tested,” he recalls.

a5455.speaker: Bank of Namibia
a5455.name: Bank of Namibia
a5455.speech: According to the Bank of Namibia, the oil and gas sector generated N$33.4 billion in FDI inflows between 2021 and 2023.

a5455.speaker: Vision 2030 (Namibian national development document)
a5455.name: Vision 2030 (Namibian national development document)
a5455.speech: Namibia's industrial ambition is articulated in Vision 2030, which stipulates that the country should be an industrialised nation with high income by the year 2030.

a5502.speaker: Dr. Abdulaziz Othman Altwaijri, Director-General of ISESCO and Secretary-General of the Federation of the Universities of the Islamic World
a5502.name: Dr. Abdulaziz Othman Altwaijri
a5502.title: Director-General of ISESCO and Secretary-General of the Federation of the Universities of the Islamic World
a5502.speech: In an address on the occasion, expressed his happiness at being granted this degree, with which he was honoured by the University of Letters and Human Sciences in Bamako, which he described as a towering scholarly edifice in the Republic of Mali and in the African region ; said that this noble initiative by the university is an honour of deep significance for him personally, for ISESCO, and for the Federation of the Universities of the Islamic World.

a5502.speaker: Dr. Abdulaziz Othman Altwaijri, Director-General of ISESCO
a5502.name: Dr. Abdulaziz Othman Altwaijri
a5502.title: Director-General of ISESCO
a5502.speech: Delivered a lecture entitled “Islamic Diplomacy in the Service of Peace”, addressing the definition of diplomacy linguistically and technically, diplomacy in Islamic history and within joint Islamic action, the international concept of diplomacy, the founding stages of Islamic diplomacy, and the emergence of international relations and the diplomacy of dialogue and peace, as well as ISESCO's role in the service of Islamic diplomacy ; explained the concept of Islamic diplomacy from the legal perspective of diplomacy and international relations within the international political order, on the basis of the Islamic principles on which it rests and proceeding from Islamic solidarity, highlighting what distinguishes Islamic diplomacy as carrying a faith-based, humanitarian message that serves the causes of dialogue and peace.

a5502.speaker: Dr. Abdulaziz Othman Altwaijri, Director-General of ISESCO
a5502.name: Dr. Abdulaziz Othman Altwaijri
a5502.title: Director-General of ISESCO
a5502.speech: In a working session with ministers and senior officials of the Government of Mali, gave a comprehensive presentation reviewing the main lines of ISESCO's plan of action for 2013-2015 in various fields; the two sides agreed to prepare joint programmes and projects to be implemented within the plan of action for 2016-2018.

a5569.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5569.name: Donald Trump
a5569.title: US President
a5569.speech: Told the US Congress on Tuesday that Lesotho is a country "nobody has ever heard of" ; addressing a joint session of Congress, announced: "We will be ending the flagrant wasting of taxpayers' dollars and to that end, I have created a brand-new Department of Government Efficiency, DOGE - perhaps you've heard of it - which is headed by Elon Musk, who is in the gallery tonight." ; "Thank you, Elon, you have worked very hard," adding: "Just listen to some of the appalling waste we have already identified." ; listed various foreign aid initiatives, including "$8 million to promote LGBTQI+ rights in the African nation of Lesotho, which nobody has ever heard of".

a5569.speaker: GroundUp (news outlet)
a5569.name: GroundUp (news outlet)
a5569.speech: Reported Trump's remarks to Congress and reported on the Starlink Lesotho licence application, including that, according to application documents seen by GroundUp, the application was submitted on 24 January by Micaela Pawlak, listed on LinkedIn as Starlink's market access manager at SpaceX.

a5569.speaker: Richard Jinu Lee, director of Starlink Lesotho (letter dated 18 April 2024)
a5569.name: Richard Jinu Lee
a5569.title: director of Starlink Lesotho (letter dated 18 April 2024)
a5569.speech: Confirmed SpaceX's economic support for Starlink Lesotho.

a5569.speaker: Lesotho Communications Authority (LCA)
a5569.name: Lesotho Communications Authority (LCA)
a5569.speech: Is currently consulting the public on whether Starlink Lesotho Pty Ltd should be granted a licence to operate in the country; in February issued a public notice confirming receipt of Starlink Lesotho's application for a Network Services Licence, which if approved would be valid for 10 years, and has invited comments in writing.

a5569.speaker: Starlink Lesotho / SpaceX (licence application)
a5569.name: Starlink Lesotho / SpaceX (licence application)
a5569.speech: Highlighted its potential to advance Lesotho's connectivity goals: "With Starlink, SpaceX can provide connectivity that reduces infrastructure investment and complements traditional internet service providers." ; "Since receiving authorisation, SpaceX has deployed over 7 000 satellites and is already providing reliable, low-latency, high-speed broadband services in multiple markets across Europe, the Americas, Africa, Asia, and Oceania. Many additional markets are targeted for service introduction in 2025 and beyond."

a5569.speaker: One Thousand & One Voices (US-based private family capital fund)
a5569.name: One Thousand & One Voices (US-based private family capital fund)
a5569.speech: Says it has also invested in the Lesotho-based Rosehip Company.

a5569.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Lesotho
a5569.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a5569.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Lesotho
a5569.speech: Speaking to GroundUp, acknowledged the US' right to cut aid to Lesotho: "The funding came through negotiations and agreements. If the US decides to terminate those agreements, there is nothing we can do but accept it." ; "Taking measures [against the US] could drag us into disputes with someone who deliberately wants to drag us into the mud." ; "We have seen his approach to international issues and how he addresses other countries. Just recently, he was asking how much it would cost to buy Greenland. So, taking any steps now could be a waste of time for us." ; "For him to speak that way about Lesotho is quite unfortunate. We are disappointed to be referred to in such a manner by a head of state."

a5660.speaker: Luísa Meque, chairperson of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a5660.name: Luísa Meque
a5660.title: chairperson of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a5660.speech: Speaking on Tuesday in Maputo during the launch of the PEGDI, said over 800,000 people are displaced in the country: “We refer to the destruction of homes, where families have lost their possessions, some due to terrorism, others because they have suffered from the impacts of cyclones. Natural disasters have affected many families” ; said these figures are worrying and there is a need to boost humanitarian assistance; also revealed that, during the peak of the terrorist attacks in Cabo Delgado, around 1.4 million people were displaced, of whom around 600,000 have already returned to their areas of origin.

a5660.speaker: Luísa Meque, chairperson of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a5660.name: Luísa Meque
a5660.title: chairperson of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a5660.speech: On the PEGDI plan: “we hope to reduce the number of people at risk of displacement and create a favorable environment to find lasting solutions, through the provision of essential services during their return, local integration and integration elsewhere in the country” ; “This plan defines actions to respond to internal displacement and poverty reduction in terms of access to basic social services such as education, health, sanitation and water supply, social inclusion and security, as well as economic protection and opportunities.”

a5660.speaker: UNDP in Mozambique (@UNDPMozambique, social media post)
a5660.name: UNDP in Mozambique (@UNDPMozambique
a5660.title: social media post)
a5660.speech: “INGD launches National Action Plan #PEGDI 2025-2029! A roadmap to manage internal displacement & reduce poverty through: Prevention & Mitigation, Prevention & Preparedness, Response, Reconstruction & Recovery. A step toward resilience & inclusive growth for displaced…”

a5717.speaker: Charles Kafunda, Principal Resident Magistrate (court ruling)
a5717.name: Charles Kafunda
a5717.title: Principal Resident Magistrate (court ruling)
a5717.speech: Convicted and sentenced Mrs. Chiluba on four counts; told a courtroom packed with Chiluba supporters that she had failed to explain how she had received the questionable properties and goods. ; "These were serious allegations and were casually explained by the accused, and I now convict you accordingly and sentence you to three-and-a-half years simple imprisonment."

a5717.speaker: Frederick Chiluba, former Zambian President
a5717.name: Frederick Chiluba
a5717.title: former Zambian President
a5717.speech: As he left the court, said his wife's sentence would just be a "passing phase."

a5903.speaker: UNICEF (statement)
a5903.name: UNICEF (statement)
a5903.speech: “UNICEF is recording record levels of admissions for treatment of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) - the deadliest form of malnutrition - in the areas that humanitarian assistance can reach” ; but “conditions in areas inaccessible because of the fighting - where children have the most urgent needs - are without doubt worse” ; an estimated 3.5 million children are expected to suffer acute malnutrition this year, including more than 700,000 expected to suffer from SAM and to need specialised, uninterrupted, life-saving treatment.

a5903.speaker: UNICEF (statement)
a5903.name: UNICEF (statement)
a5903.speech: Highlights that some three million children are internally displaced in the country since the start of the armed conflict of almost 300 days – in addition to the two million people already displaced from earlier crises – making this “the largest number of internally displaced children in the world” ; reveals that health workers have not been paid for months in Sudan, that more than 70% of health facilities in areas affected by clashes no longer function, and that two thirds of the population have no access to health care ; “The number of cholera cases alone has more than doubled in the last month, with more than 10,000 suspected cases and 300 deaths, 16% among children under 5, recorded at the end of January.”

a5903.speaker: Catherine Russell, Executive Director of UNICEF
a5903.name: Catherine Russell
a5903.title: Executive Director of UNICEF
a5903.speech: “We have an extremely short window to prevent a massive loss of life”, calling for safe access to conflict zones and for international aid.

a5903.speaker: Most recent food security analysis in Sudan (report)
a5903.name: Most recent food security analysis in Sudan (report)
a5903.speech: Revealed “the highest levels of hunger ever recorded during the October to February harvest season”, after the recent spread of insecurity to Al Jazira state, the country’s breadbasket.

a5903.speaker: UNICEF (statement)
a5903.name: UNICEF (statement)
a5903.speech: Considers that “parts of Khartoum, Kordofan and Darfur will face a high risk of catastrophic hunger conditions in the coming lean season, which could begin as early as March this year” if there is no significant increase in international aid ; adds that “it is particularly critical to get humanitarian supplies into Darfur”, the scene of some of the worst fighting, an area hosting more than a third of the displaced population and where more than 200,000 children are expected to suffer from SAM.

a5903.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a5903.name: United Nations (UN)
a5903.speech: Announced that the parties to the conflict in Sudan have agreed to meet under UN auspices to discuss humanitarian aid, on a date yet to be determined ; declared the same day that it needed 4.1 billion dollars (3.8 billion euros) to meet the humanitarian needs of the population of Sudan and of Sudanese who have fled to neighbouring countries.

a6009.speaker: Residents living close to Khartoum International Airport
a6009.name: Residents living close to Khartoum International Airport
a6009.speech: Told Al Jazeera that drones and surface-to-air missiles were heard above the capital in the early hours of Friday morning, before loud explosions went off.

a6009.speaker: Airport official (anonymous)
a6009.name: Airport official (anonymous)
a6009.speech: Told AFP on condition of anonymity that the airport's reopening has been postponed "under further notice" because of incoming attacks.

a6009.speaker: Hiba Morgan, Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Khartoum
a6009.name: Hiba Morgan
a6009.title: Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Khartoum
a6009.speech: Said that "despite authorities saying that operations are scheduled to start on October 26, there are concerns that this will not happen."

a6009.speaker: Alfatih Bashir, Omdurman resident
a6009.name: Alfatih Bashir
a6009.title: Omdurman resident
a6009.speech: "I built it when I was working abroad," Bashir told Al Jazeera of his house, which has collapsed ceilings and damaged walls, adding that now he did not possess the necessary funds to repair the damage ; "I'm not working, I'm just sitting idly with my wife and two children. We sometimes barely have enough to eat. How can I even start to rebuild?"

a6009.speaker: Afaf Khamed, resident
a6009.name: Afaf Khamed
a6009.title: resident
a6009.speech: Said she fainted when she saw the extent of the damage ; "This house is where we were born, where all our family members got married. I now live here with my sister, and we can't rebuild because we don't have anyone to help us."

a6009.speaker: Mohammed Ali, shop owner
a6009.name: Mohammed Ali
a6009.title: shop owner
a6009.speech: Said materials take too long to arrive because of security checks, and that makes them more expensive; as a consequence, "fewer and fewer people are coming to buy building materials."

a6009.speaker: Sudan's government
a6009.name: Sudan's government
a6009.speech: Has pledged to rebuild the capital, but its focus so far has been on state institutions, while residents are left to figure out how to rebuild on their own.

a6072.speaker: Authorities in Sofala Province
a6072.name: Authorities in Sofala Province
a6072.speech: According to the authorities in the province, the El Nino phenomenon and the poor performance of the cotton company that assists producers contributed to the failure of the work (the missed cotton and oilseed production target).

a6072.speaker: The perpetrators of the attack in Mogovolas district (unidentified)
a6072.name: The perpetrators of the attack in Mogovolas district (unidentified)
a6072.speech: Allege that the health sector is spreading the cholera vibrio, the virus that causes cholera, the disease that has broken out in that region of Nampula.

a6072.speaker: Televisao de Mocambique (TVM)
a6072.name: Televisao de Mocambique (TVM)
a6072.speech: Condemns the use of its institutional brand for the spread of disinformation on social media. The most recent case was the circulation of a doctored image, unconnected to TVM, accusing the channel of having reported the running over, this Wednesday, of a young woman by a BTR military vehicle.

a6072.speaker: Players of Chingale de Tete
a6072.name: Players of Chingale de Tete
a6072.speech: Are not carried away by euphoria; they are asking for support in the stands in Saturday's high-risk match.

a6072.speaker: National Institute of Meteorology (INAM)
a6072.name: National Institute of Meteorology (INAM)
a6072.speech: Forecasts from today the occurrence of heavy rains of more than seventy-five millimetres in 24 hours, accompanied by thunderstorms and strong winds in the provinces of Sofala, Manica, Tete, Zambezia and Nampula; according to INAM, the northern and central provinces and the southern coastal strip will record moderate, locally heavy rainfall during the same period ; INAM recommends precautionary and safety measures.

a6072.speaker: Citizens in Beira
a6072.name: Citizens in Beira
a6072.speech: Are calling for an end to the demonstrations in the country. They consider that, although it is a constitutional right, the way in which they take place violates other rights of citizens.

a6254.speaker: Mark Steyn, Canadian newspaper columnist and author of “America Alone: The End of the World as We Know It”
a6254.name: Mark Steyn
a6254.title: Canadian newspaper columnist and author of “America Alone: The End of the World as We Know It”
a6254.speech: Thought demographic shifts, cultural decline, and Islam would ruin Western civilisation, and that the only redeeming grace was American exceptionalism.

a6254.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6254.name: Donald Trump
a6254.title: US President
a6254.speech: Accused Mexico and Canada of not doing enough to control the flow of fentanyl into the US, and accused Beijing, in addition to his perennial accusations of stealing US technology and other unfair trade practices, of sending ingredients for making fentanyl to Mexico.

a6254.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6254.name: Donald Trump
a6254.title: US President
a6254.speech: Said in his second inaugural address that his “proudest legacy will be that of a peacemaker and unifier” ; spoke of a redemptive mission for aliens in some parts of the US now reduced to “eating the dogs and the pets.”

a6254.speaker: Analysts
a6254.name: Analysts
a6254.speech: Before the one-month tariff pause between the US and its neighbours, forecast the tariffs would hinder US GDP growth by approximately 0.25% to 0.3%, that the tariffs on Canada and Mexico alone could decrease overall economic output by around $45 billion, with potential losses escalating to $75 billion following retaliatory measures.

a6270.speaker: 2025 World Happiness Report
a6270.name: 2025 World Happiness Report
a6270.speech: Showed that Nigeria dropped three spots from its 2024 ranking of 102 but has moved higher to become the 10th happiest country in Africa; according to the report, the Netherlands ranks fifth, Israel number eight, and Luxembourg number nine, completing the top 10 list; it examines how happiness varies across populations, showing significant differences within and between nations; the report looks at six key variables to help explain life evaluations: GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption; this year’s edition focused “on the impact of caring and sharing on people’s happiness”.

a6270.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a6270.name: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a6270.speech: Reports that the International Day of Happiness, celebrated annually on March 20 since 2013, coincides with the release of the yearly report.

a6295.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a6295.name: Nangolo Mbumba
a6295.title: President of Namibia
a6295.speech: "Our elections are over; it was tough, it was complicated, and everybody saw what happened, but now we have a President-elect in the capacity of Dr. Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah. She will have time to organise her things because, according to our rules, having started from the year we gained our independence, we had elections in November 1989, and we needed 3 months to draft the Constitution, and that is why our independence is in March, and because of that we always have elections in November. But the assumption of power is in March. Nevertheless, we are comfortable now that when the dust has settled, everybody will accept what we have gotten from the people of Namibia. We have solid bilateral relations. We are benefiting from PEPFAR in terms of health, AGOA in terms of trade, YALI, and the Peace Corps."

a6295.speaker: Randy Berry, US Ambassador to Namibia
a6295.name: Randy Berry
a6295.title: US Ambassador to Namibia
a6295.speech: Informed President Mbumba: "I also had a chance to discuss with the President how much I believe that is intensifying rapidly. I think all of the elements for closer relationships for increased coordination and collaboration are based on those very items, and when you are talking about democracies, democracies are driven by the rule of law, driven by institutions, and they are driven by elections, and those bring us together in terms of making sure that people's voices are heard. One area where I see a great deal of hope is expanding the economic situation; obviously, Namibians want opportunities; they want an economy that is thriving. We have seen a significant increase in private-sector investment from US firms here."

a6388.speaker: Haakon Gram-Johannessen, Norwegian Ambassador to Mozambique, and Greg Carr, President of the Gorongosa Restoration Project
a6388.name: Haakon Gram-Johannessen
a6388.title: Norwegian Ambassador to Mozambique, and Greg Carr, President of the Gorongosa Restoration Project
a6388.speech: On the occasion, both expressed their satisfaction with the initiative and hope regarding the increase in Gorongosa Coffee production.

a6388.speaker: Gorongosa Project (press release)
a6388.name: Gorongosa Project (press release)
a6388.speech: States that it works with the central government of Mozambique and with Sofala Province and district representatives of those ministries, and with traditional leaders in community “regulados” through Natural Resource Management Committees ; “We collaborate with UN-Habitat, the Red Cross and the World Food Program. We receive support and advice from partners such as USAID, Netherlands, Ireland, Norway, Canada, Portugal, EU, HHMI, among others.”

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: Said the consultations in Moscow between the three AES foreign ministers and Sergei Lavrov showed that Russia and the AES countries share a common vision of their international engagement, based on respect for the sovereignty of their countries, respect for their sovereign choices, and consideration of the interests of their populations, and on the fact that their countries work internationally so that their voice is heard "to combat together imperialism, neocolonialism, the subjugation of our countries, the instrumentalization of human rights," and the rejection of interference in countries' internal affairs.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: Said they also wanted to build a strategic partnership between Russia and the AES covering three areas: first peace and security — the essential question that gave rise to the Confederation of Sahel States — with Russia asked to support the Confederation's joint military operations and, later, the establishment of a unified AES force; second diplomacy, allowing the countries to speak with one voice internationally, noting that "Russia needs our countries, we need Russia as a permanent member of the UN Security Council," which has supported them against unjust international actions while they support Russia when it asks; and third development, including economic integration, railways, road infrastructure, energy, agricultural and mining projects, and an investment bank to generate own resources ; said the exchanges were very frank and open, that Russia showed a very strong commitment, and that they agreed to institutionalize the consultation mechanism with meetings at least once a year, alternating between Russia and the AES space, the next one in the AES space early next year, with a follow-up mechanism in place — an important step consolidating their ties and reflecting growing recognition by bilateral and multilateral actors of the AES as a geopolitical reality.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On whether an AES-Russia summit is planned, said it is not excluded a priori and was not openly discussed, but the mechanism exists and it is possible depending on the heads of state's guidance ; said President Vladimir Putin and the AES heads of state — Captain Ibrahim Traoré of Burkina Faso, General Abdourahamane Tchiani of Niger, and General Assimi Goïta of Mali — have much in common, share a vision of their countries' concerns and consult regularly, and he does not rule out that one day they decide to meet in that framework ; said the ministers with Sergei Lavrov, and their ambassadors, will continue this political animation and consultation to obtain concrete results for their populations in a spirit of win-win partnership with Russia.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On military autonomy, said they already work with Russia on several projects and their countries wish to strengthen capacities and develop autonomy "so that we get out of patterns of dependence" ; said the acquisition of military equipment will be a growing need and their countries will not remain in a dynamic of simply continuing to import military equipment, so technology transfer and strengthening of processing capacities with the Russian partner — who is not opposed to it — are important; noted President Goïta's ambition to develop a military industry in Mali and the AES-wide will to establish processing capacities, which would reduce dependence on imports, create jobs, and reinforce the vision of industrialization and structural transformation of their economies.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On the common AES visa policy, said these questions fall within their desire to strengthen the free movement of citizens in their space and to facilitate the movement of visitors, tourists and partners; the visa question is an initiative of the heads of state, experts have analyzed it and made proposals, and it is now on the ministers' table as a project under way ; on the AES passport, said there is also the AES biometric identity card to allow citizens to move within a fairly complex security environment; the passport was adopted in January by Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, and technically contains norms and specifications going beyond what is normally required by ICAO; notification with technical specifications and physical specimens was made to ICAO, based in Canada, and to all concerned states, first for the ordinary passport and then for diplomatic and service passports; "To date we have recorded no rejection by any country of this passport," though processing times vary from country to country, so the debate over international recognition of the AES passport "has no reason to be," and he assures that the passport meets the highest standards of security and reliability.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On the 0.5% confederal levy on imports from third countries, said the question is not new — the same mechanism was used by ECOWAS for its financing — and now that their countries are no longer ECOWAS members they have put in place a confederal levy directing the same resources to finance the Confederation of Sahel States: first its operation, then some of its institutions such as the investment bank, and a number of structuring projects ; said this fits the heads of state's vision that the structures and organizations they establish should not be financed by external partners, because that ultimately authorizes those partners to control their organizations and dictate their agenda: "We must count on ourselves," prioritizing their own resources, which does not mean the AES will not work with certain partners on certain projects, but it will do so without being dependent on external financing and above all without letting such financing allow other actors to take control.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
