a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On further fiscal measures, said he is not necessarily responsible for these questions, but that as a matter of principle their countries and citizens must be ready to assume greater financial responsibilities ; said the international system itself faces challenges such that, because of wars, tensions or geopolitical considerations, resources for financing development or humanitarian action are becoming increasingly scarce, so it will fall to their countries to identify innovative sources of financing or mobilize more domestic resources, in a systemic approach to development financing.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On the AES countries' withdrawal from the OIF, said calling it a cultural break is going too far: there are historical links between France and their countries, even if formed in circumstances that do not necessarily honour them because they are linked to colonization ; said speaking French is a colonial heritage, while the OIF, created in 1970, is a political organization among countries that share French — some members barely speak it — and in leaving, their countries did not decide to cut ties with French-speaking countries but to leave an organization under the influence of one particular country that promotes the language, since their countries do not aim to perpetuate this colonial heritage ; said the main reason for withdrawal was the organization's double standards: their countries were suspended for breach of constitutional order, which is in the texts and which they do not deny, but in the same situations in the same countries treatment differs depending on whether a country's relationship with France is calm or tense, which is unacceptable — they cannot pay their dues and have their three countries treated differently on political or geopolitical grounds, or because decisions are remote-controlled by a country that has tensions with them; on principle they are against sanctions, but if applied they must be balanced ; said their countries spoke French before the OIF was created and will continue to speak it as a colonial heritage; under Mali's new constitution French is a working language, a needed tool, but the national languages now have the status of official language, and promoting them more is an important objective; President Goïta has decreed this the year of culture, and culture is best conveyed in national languages; Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger share national languages and can work to valorize them and position themselves in a multilingualism allowing them to speak English, Russian, Chinese or other languages, using a language as a commercial vehicle rather than taking responsibility for promoting any language or country.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On possible Russian help preserving and promoting Mali's local languages, said it is an objective they welcome and a laudable one if Russian experts or the Russian state decide to work with their countries to promote their languages alongside Russian, and they remain open to it ; said promotion of national languages is a political objective and high priority, and while they are not closed to working languages such as Russian, French or English because they need them, the priority is the national languages that allow them to valorize their cultures and identity, since the vast majority of their citizens express themselves far more in those languages than in foreign ones.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On the growth of Russian-language learning in the Sahel through partner Russian Houses, said cultural relations with Russia are not new but date from the first years of their independence, with thousands of Malians who speak Russian having studied in the former USSR and in Russia ; said they encourage all efforts allowing the acquisition of other languages, that Russian as a working language would also foster exchanges and mutual understanding between Russia and their countries, and that this can only help the Russian people and the peoples of the AES share common values and work for the advent of world peace.

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On the US halting the USAID programme, said: "Personally, I am not destabilized by this decision. Moreover, the government of Mali is not destabilized either." ; said the first lesson is that for some months they had been in discussion with USAID in Mali, discussions that were very difficult and reached a deadlock, because the way American aid was dispensed in Mali did not allow Malians to choose the priorities, did not allow Malians to choose the NGOs selected to implement it, and the resources in question did not even pass through the state budget — a matter Mali objected to out of concern for national ownership; if a foreign partner is to execute programmes in Mali it must be done with the state or in agreement with the Malian state ; said the second lesson is that countries that suddenly decide to suspend their aid show that the aid was not coming for their populations, but that aid is a political instrument or an instrument of foreign policy to achieve certain objectives, and if they judge those objectives unattainable they can change ; said the third lesson is that their countries must be realistic and cannot build their plans on the interests of others: such aid is destined one day to dry up or diminish, because countries demand things — because they were not voted with in a certain direction, or for some other reason, or because of political changes — and then decide not to provide it ; said they must therefore find the mechanisms to finance their countries with internal resources and identify international resources that are not necessarily subject to these political diktats, noting frameworks such as the BRICS that allow access to resources free of political conditionalities that handicap their development ; said: "Today it is USAID, yesterday it was Sweden in Mali's case, tomorrow it will be another country. So these are not isolated incidents, it is part of a pattern. It is up to us to understand that this aid pursues political objectives and will depend on political conditionalities that may or may not be acceptable to us."

a6436.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a6436.title: Foreign Minister of Mali
a6436.speech: On the limited Russia-Ukraine ceasefire covering energy infrastructure and Black Sea navigation, said peace between Russia and Ukraine would benefit the whole world, stability, the global economy and their own countries' economies, so it is something they support, and they encourage Russia to pursue its efforts to establish peace with its neighbour ; said Mali expresses its solidarity with Russia, as does the AES, in this struggle, and they hope to move forward together to find peace ; said Mali has broken off relations with Ukraine and considers Ukraine a terrorist state insofar as Ukraine openly claimed support for terrorist groups in the Sahel and particularly in Mali, causing the deaths of many Malian soldiers and citizens; they condemn this act and consider that Ukraine must assume its responsibilities and be treated by African peoples as a troublemaker in their space, an irresponsible actor creating insecurity in their regions ; said this does not prevent them from wishing for peace between Russia and Ukraine, and that if such peace makes it easier to move Ukrainian or Russian production to populations and countries that need it, that is an excellent thing; Mali and the AES generally favour all initiatives leading to peace, but a just and lasting peace that takes account of Russia's security concerns.

a6635.speaker: World Bank and Global Wildlife Program (Collaborative Management Partnership Toolkit / resource guide)
a6635.name: World Bank and Global Wildlife Program (Collaborative Management Partnership Toolkit / resource guide)
a6635.speech: A landmark new resource guide and toolkit features Mozambique’s Gorongosa National Park as a successful case study and model of a “Collaborative Management Partnership” – a public-private agreement set up to manage conservation areas and support sustainable, inclusive development; it raises awareness of partnership experiences in Africa and highlights best practices, benefits, challenges, and lessons learned.

a6635.speaker: Researchers (cited in the report)
a6635.name: Researchers (cited in the report)
a6635.speech: Found that an additional $1.5 billion is needed annually to effectively manage conservation areas with lions in Africa ; found the median funding for these areas in Africa is almost three times greater with public-private partnerships.

a6635.speaker: Dominique Gonçalves, Manager of the Gorongosa National Park Elephant Ecology Project
a6635.name: Dominique Gonçalves
a6635.title: Manager of the Gorongosa National Park Elephant Ecology Project
a6635.speech: “I hope that the Gorongosa model creates new advocates and funders for integrated conservation and development projects in Mozambique and Africa by promoting a positive new vision of African national parks as ‘engines of sustainable human development.”

a6722.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a6722.name: Donald Trump
a6722.title: US President-elect
a6722.speech: Said on Tuesday that he intends to discuss with Russian President Vladimir Putin the efforts to be considered in order to end the war in Ukraine; speaking at a press conference from his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, he suggested such a meeting could take place after his inauguration on 20 January and, asked about the timing, refrained from giving a precise date but said: “I know Putin would like a meeting.”

a6722.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a6722.name: Donald Trump
a6722.title: US President-elect
a6722.speech: Reaffirmed his hope that Russia’s war of invasion in Ukraine will end within six months: “I hope well before six months” ; during his campaign he often boasted of his relationship with the Russian president and claimed he could end the war in Ukraine “in 24 hours”, without ever revealing details of that claim.

a6722.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a6722.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a6722.title: Ukrainian President
a6722.speech: In his New Year’s address, appealed to Washington not to reduce aid to Ukraine.

a6769.speaker: Mike Mansfield, US Ambassador to Japan
a6769.name: Mike Mansfield
a6769.title: US Ambassador to Japan
a6769.speech: Would start every speech he gave in Japan with the admonition: "As I have often said, the US-Japan relationship is the single most important bilateral relationship in the world today, bar none."

a6769.speaker: Robert Gates, former US Secretary of Defence
a6769.name: Robert Gates
a6769.title: former US Secretary of Defence
a6769.speech: Had done something virtually unknown in Washington by warning that the prevailing budgetary pattern was unsustainable once Afghanistan and Iraq no longer drained the treasury.

a6769.speaker: Leon Panetta, US Secretary of Defence
a6769.name: Leon Panetta
a6769.title: US Secretary of Defence
a6769.speech: Told a Japanese military audience at America's Yokota Air Force Base near Tokyo: "I want to make very clear that the United States is going to remain a presence in the Pacific for a long time. That means, just so you understand, that we are not anticipating any cutbacks in this region. If anything, we're going to strengthen our presence in the Pacific."

a6769.speaker: The New York Times
a6769.name: The New York Times
a6769.speech: Added that Panetta's message "...Is the new call of the Obama administration as it winds down the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan and scrambles to project its power in Asia. But this eastward pivot, meant to shore up Asian alliances and send a clear signal that the US opposes China's claims to island territories far beyond its shores, comes at a difficult time. Like everyone else, Asian allies see an ailing American economy and coming Pentagon budget cuts - at least $450 billion over the next decade - and a growing isolationism among Republicans eager for the White House."

a6769.speaker: Other Pentagon officials (unnamed)
a6769.name: Other Pentagon officials (unnamed)
a6769.speech: Told the media the US still had no plans to reduce the 85,000 military personnel around the Pacific, let alone draw down on the seven aircraft carrier battle groups that patrol the region.

a6769.speaker: US defence officials (unnamed)
a6769.name: US defence officials (unnamed)
a6769.speech: Say that automatic across-the-board reductions of a further $600 billion from the Pentagon could force real military reductions in the Pacific even as China is expanding its own capabilities.

a6769.speaker: The Chinese (government)
a6769.name: The Chinese (government)
a6769.speech: Argue their own modernisation programme is an essential upgrading after decades of subordinating defence expenditures to civilian needs and, in any case, that their build-up is essential to counter the American presence.

a6769.speaker: Sun Zhe, director of Tsinghua University's Centre on United States-China relations
a6769.name: Sun Zhe
a6769.title: director of Tsinghua University's Centre on United States-China relations
a6769.speech: "It's a serious threat and a potential threat. If you say they [the US' seven carriers and 18 nuclear subs in the region] are only targeting North Korea, nobody will believe it."

a6769.speaker: Michael Schiffer, US deputy assistant secretary of defence for East Asia
a6769.name: Michael Schiffer
a6769.title: US deputy assistant secretary of defence for East Asia
a6769.speech: "The pace and scope of China's sustained military investments have allowed China to pursue capabilities we believe are potentially destabilising to regional military balances, increase the risk of misunderstanding and miscalculation and may contribute to regional tensions and anxieties."

a6769.speaker: Roy Kamphausen, China expert at the National Bureau of Asian Research and former China specialist at the Pentagon
a6769.name: Roy Kamphausen
a6769.title: China expert at the National Bureau of Asian Research and former China specialist at the Pentagon
a6769.speech: Argues: "We trivialise that challenge if we focus exclusively on the military modernisation programme. Our navy and air force need to modernise for their own reasons and not just on the basis of a nascent Chinese threat."

a6769.speaker: Hillary Clinton, US Secretary of State (in Foreign Policy magazine)
a6769.name: Hillary Clinton
a6769.title: US Secretary of State (in Foreign Policy magazine)
a6769.speech: Set out the message that over the coming decade, the US needs "a substantially increased investment - diplomatic, economic, strategic and otherwise."

a6769.speaker: Mitt Romney, US Republican presidential candidate
a6769.name: Mitt Romney
a6769.title: US Republican presidential candidate
a6769.speech: Recently argued China should be forced to spend more on foreign aid, rather than lending the US money by buying its government bonds so America can ship all that cash to poorer foreign nations.

a6769.speaker: Rick Perry and Ron Paul, US Republican presidential candidates
a6769.name: Rick Perry and Ron Paul
a6769.title: US Republican presidential candidates
a6769.speech: Utterances that speak to a new kind of neo-isolationism in international affairs and draw-downs of US forces abroad.

a6825.speaker: Zhao Weiping, China’s Ambassador to Namibia
a6825.name: Zhao Weiping
a6825.title: China’s Ambassador to Namibia
a6825.speech: Says he does not agree with the view that China provides developmental assistance to African countries in favour of getting its hands on its mineral resources, emphasising the win-win cooperation between Africa and China: “We provide development assistance to our African friends because we are the largest developing country and the second largest economy in the world. So we just think it’s something we should do to help our African friends. We never attach any political conditions to our assistance, and we never use our assistance to seek any special favour in return. So this summit, I think has, of course, reflected the win-win spirit. But for me, more importantly, I think it is also reflected in China, Africa, friendship, and we all belong to the global south, and the global south countries should help each other to boost our overall position in international politics.”

a6844.speaker: HIV response researchers (experts addressing the press ahead of the IAS 2025 Conference)
a6844.name: HIV response researchers (experts addressing the press ahead of the IAS 2025 Conference)
a6844.speech: Have sounded the alarm over recent global funding cuts, saying they have severely disrupted efforts to combat HIV, threatening life-saving research, prevention and treatment; presented scientific highlights from four studies selected from abstracts being showcased at the conference, revealing predictive modelling and real-world data from Africa and Latin America, indicating rising HIV acquisitions, stalled treatment and fragile health systems.

a6844.speaker: Dr Beatriz Grinsztejn, IAS president
a6844.name: Dr Beatriz Grinsztejn
a6844.title: IAS president
a6844.speech: Said that, on one hand, the world is witnessing extraordinary scientific breakthroughs that could transform prevention and treatment and “even bring us closer to a cure” ; “On the other hand, these very advances are under threat from massive funding cuts that risk stalling clinical trials, slowing our progress and jeopardising the achievements we’ve fought so hard to attain.”

a6844.speaker: Professor Kenneth Ngure, IAS president-elect
a6844.name: Professor Kenneth Ngure
a6844.title: IAS president-elect
a6844.speech: Said that the sudden cuts to United States (US) funding, announced earlier this year, have been “deeply felt” across the African continent by millions of people who rely on HIV prevention, testing and treatment services.

a6844.speaker: Preprint modelling study presented by lead author Dr Jack Stone, Associate Professor in Infectious Disease Mathematical Modelling at the University of Bristol
a6844.name: Preprint modelling study presented by lead author Dr Jack Stone
a6844.title: Associate Professor in Infectious Disease Mathematical Modelling at the University of Bristol
a6844.speech: Finds that HIV incidence and related deaths are expected to rise significantly in sub-Saharan Africa due to disruptions in funding for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) under Pepfar; suggests that the pause in PrEP funding from January 2025 — after PEPFAR-funded PrEP had been accessed by nearly 700,000 people across 28 sub-Saharan African countries, including Malawi, by late 2024 — could result in approximately 6,671 additional HIV acquisitions over one year, and a further 3,617 cases over the subsequent five years, with more than 2,900 of these additional cases projected among gay and bisexual men who have sex with men and over 2,000 among female sex workers.

a6844.speaker: Dr Jack Stone, Associate Professor in Infectious Disease Mathematical Modelling at the University of Bristol
a6844.name: Dr Jack Stone
a6844.title: Associate Professor in Infectious Disease Mathematical Modelling at the University of Bristol
a6844.speech: “It is crucial that funding is secured to continue and expand PrEP services in sub-Saharan Africa.”

a6844.speaker: Zackie Achmat, founder of the Treatment Action Campaign and member of the Global HIV Treatment Coalition
a6844.name: Zackie Achmat
a6844.title: founder of the Treatment Action Campaign and member of the Global HIV Treatment Coalition
a6844.speech: Issued a call to action on the urgent need for debt refinancing to protect the HIV response in low- and middle-income countries: “You can’t end the Aids pandemic while African nations must choose between paying creditors and saving lives. As someone who has lived with HIV for more than half my life, I have seen the cost of political inaction.” ; “We fought for treatment when the world said it was impossible. Now, the convergence of crushing debt and funding cuts threatens everything we’ve built. We need urgent debt restructuring so African countries can invest in saving lives instead of servicing debt.”

a6872.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Economic Outlook (July update)
a6872.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a6872.title: World Economic Outlook (July update)
a6872.speech: has revised its global economic growth forecast for 2025 to 3.0 percent, slightly up from its April estimate; has, however, warned that the improvement is temporary and driven by short-term trade distortions rather than real fundamentals; cautioned that global growth remained below the pre-pandemic average of 3.7 percent, and risks to the outlook are “tilted to the downside”; the July update highlighted ongoing trade tensions, geopolitical instability and rising fiscal vulnerabilities in major economies as key threats.

a6872.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Economic Outlook (July update)
a6872.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a6872.title: World Economic Outlook (July update)
a6872.speech: projects growth of 4.0 percent in 2025 for sub-Saharan Africa, rising modestly to 4.3 percent in 2026, with the region's growth expected to remain stable but insufficient to absorb rising population pressures and persistent development gaps; added that countries such as Malawi, with high debt levels, could face additional borrowing constraints.

a6872.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a6872.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a6872.speech: called on governments to implement policies that restore confidence and ensure sustainability, such as pursuing transparent trade frameworks and reducing policy-induced uncertainty ; “Restoring fiscal space and ensuring sustainable public debt is crucial, even while addressing critical spending needs. Central banks must carefully calibrate monetary policies to country-specific circumstances to maintain price and financial stability amid prolonged trade tensions and evolving tariffs.”

a6872.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, economist
a6872.name: Velli Nyirongo
a6872.title: economist
a6872.speech: said Malawi was likely to feel the impact of the global economic trends outlined, given its heavy reliance on donor funding, imports and concessional borrowing ; “While there are signs of modest improvement in the global economic outlook, the overall environment remains volatile.”

a6872.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, economist
a6872.name: Velli Nyirongo
a6872.title: economist
a6872.speech: said donor countries themselves are under mounting pressure, as shifting geopolitical dynamics and changing domestic priorities in advanced economies were resulting in reductions in foreign aid.

a6921.speaker: Ministry of Trade and Industry (MoTI) of Ethiopia
a6921.name: Ministry of Trade and Industry (MoTI) of Ethiopia
a6921.speech: Is denouncing the National Bank of Ethiopia's (NBE) 'External Loan and Supplier's Credit Directives FXD/47/2017' that gives the right to foreign investors to access foreign loans at the cost of local industries.

a6921.speaker: Fetlework Gebregziabher, Minister of Trade and Industry
a6921.name: Fetlework Gebregziabher
a6921.title: Minister of Trade and Industry
a6921.speech: Told Capital that the local industries would not be excluded from such kind of scheme without a concrete reason: "Based on our stand we are not accepting that the supplier's credit scheme only serves the foreign investors," she says, "the central bank should change its approach and include all actors" ; "If there are conditions that should be changed or arranged it has to be done and include the local manufacturers to access hard currency in similar manner like the FDIs."

a6921.speaker: Fetlework Gebregziabher, Minister of Trade and Industry
a6921.name: Fetlework Gebregziabher
a6921.title: Minister of Trade and Industry
a6921.speech: Said that the suspect on misdemeanor should be the responsibility of NBE: "The central bank is the responsible body to answer on the claim of corruption on the approving process of the supplier's credit for each requests."

a6921.speaker: Local investors / local manufacturers
a6921.name: Local investors / local manufacturers
a6921.speech: Claim that they are discriminated against by a single directive of NBE, calling the directive an 'apartheid law' that is pushing local investors to leave the business and sell off to foreigners ; say they are engaged in the same business as foreign companies yet are supposed to wait for the letter of credit (LC) for their foreign currency demand to import raw material or spare parts, and that the amount of LC after a very long wait is also unsatisfactory compared with the production capacity of industries, pushing production cost very high and making it uncompetitive ; claimed that some of the manufacturers have closed their business and others reduced the number of workers due to this uncompetitive condition and lack of inputs.

a6921.speaker: Individuals who closely follow the sector (anonymous, declined to be mentioned due to the sensitivity of the case)
a6921.name: Individuals who closely follow the sector (anonymous
a6921.title: declined to be mentioned due to the sensitivity of the case)
a6921.speech: Claimed that the method for approving the supplier's credit is not clear and vulnerable to corruption, and that they suspect that every approval may have a link of illegality.

a6921.speaker: Experts who know the scheme
a6921.name: Experts who know the scheme
a6921.speech: Said the supplier's credit approval process is undertaken on a one-to-one approach from companies and a representative of NBE.

a6921.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (non-response)
a6921.name: Yinager Dessie
a6921.title: Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (non-response)
a6921.speech: Capital tried to talk to Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE, about the case via phone but it was unfruitful.

a6921.speaker: Sector actors
a6921.name: Sector actors
a6921.speech: Frequently claimed that the NBE directive is issued against the investment proclamation, which was amended in 2012, noting that investment proclamation no. 769 defined 'investor' as both domestic and foreign and that article 36 stated that an investor who acquires an external loan shall have such loan registered with the National Bank of Ethiopia in accordance with the directive of the bank: "Both articles of the investment proclamation did not classify local and foreign investors," they told the government.

a6921.speaker: Ethiopian Investment Commission
a6921.name: Ethiopian Investment Commission
a6921.speech: Has a stand that investors, local or international ones, should be treated the same.

a6921.speaker: Financial experts
a6921.name: Financial experts
a6921.speech: Recently told Capital that the supplier's credit scheme not only affects local investors but the financial institutions themselves because there is a default risk from their clients.

a6921.speaker: Bankers
a6921.name: Bankers
a6921.speech: Say getting the letter of credit up front breaches the first come first serve directive of the National Bank of Ethiopia ; "When the banks secure hard currency they focus on settling the credit rather than approving the LC for its other clients who are not included on the supplier's credit scheme, which is also another effect on local investors."

a6921.speaker: Prominent private bank president (anonymous, requested anonymity)
a6921.name: Prominent private bank president (anonymous
a6921.title: requested anonymity)
a6921.speech: Told Capital that initially the notion of the supplier's credit indirectly forced the banks which applied without the consultation to settle the payment by the maturity date: "It has forced the banks to face a default risk which affects the country."

a6921.speaker: Government of Ethiopia
a6921.name: Government of Ethiopia
a6921.speech: Recently stated that in the past three quarters of the budget year the government allocated USD 6 billion for the private sector.

a6921.speaker: Local manufacturers
a6921.name: Local manufacturers
a6921.speech: Argued that from the stated amount the local investors may access only six percent or USD 300 million, being the USD 200 million recently released by Commercial Bank of Ethiopia and USD 100 million via private banks for the first time.

a6963.speaker: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Spain to Mali
a6963.name: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo
a6963.title: Ambassador of the Kingdom of Spain to Mali
a6963.speech: "Thank you for the opportunity to announce the Spanish government's commitment to food security in the Sahel and in Mali in particular. I am also pleased to inform you that the Spanish cooperation agency has granted 3 million euros to the WFP in support of the CSA. In total, Spain's projected humanitarian aid to Mali this year will be about 7 million euros." ; "Spain works with the WFP as a privileged partner in all the contexts in which we work to fight food insecurity, and in Mali we are very pleased to work with the Food Security Commissioner, so the results of our support are always visible and positive."

a6963.speaker: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Spain to Mali
a6963.name: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo
a6963.title: Ambassador of the Kingdom of Spain to Mali
a6963.speech: "Nevertheless, we cannot forget that there are factors that contribute to food crises in this country and worsen the situation: violence and conflict force populations into displacement that aggravates their vulnerability, and continuous climate shocks and recurrent disasters such as floods and droughts." ; Said Spanish cooperation is also trying to contribute to improving the situation through the construction of irrigation infrastructure and the approval of food support for internally displaced people and migrants under other interventions.

a6963.speaker: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Spain to Mali
a6963.name: Antonio Guillen Hidalgo
a6963.title: Ambassador of the Kingdom of Spain to Mali
a6963.speech: "Spain supports the CSA in its determination to fight extreme hunger in Mali. We are aware of the urgent and alarming situation the country faces and I hope that this gesture will also be shared by the rest of the cooperation partners. As you know, many Malian children under 5 suffer from severe malnutrition, and the number of people needing humanitarian assistance is rising. It is to meet these challenges that Spanish cooperation has made this contribution, which is more than a donation - it is a moral obligation." ; "I am sure that the CSA, with the WFP's support, will manage well the funds made available by Spain for this noble task." ; "I hope the Spanish contribution will be a relief for the population during the lean season."

a6963.speaker: Jacqueline Flentge, WFP Deputy Country Director in Mali
a6963.name: Jacqueline Flentge
a6963.title: WFP Deputy Country Director in Mali
a6963.speech: "This new contribution, worth a total of 3 million euros, or more than 1.9 billion CFA francs, will allow us to provide vital food and nutritional assistance to thousands of vulnerable people across Mali. It will make it possible to meet immediate needs and to strengthen the resilience of the affected populations, through an integrated intervention combining emergency response with strengthening the resilience of communities vulnerable to food and nutritional insecurity." ; "It is with a feeling of deep gratitude and immense honour that I speak today, on behalf of the World Food Programme and on behalf of our country director, Gian Carlo Cirri, who is currently travelling. I therefore wish to express our most sincere appreciation to the Embassy of the Kingdom of Spain in Mali and, through it, to the government and people of the Kingdom of Spain." ; "This renewed generosity towards the World Food Programme's food insecurity response programmes is not merely financial aid. An essential investment in Mali's future, this partnership rests on fundamental shared values of solidarity and humanity."

a6963.speaker: Jacqueline Flentge, WFP Deputy Country Director in Mali
a6963.name: Jacqueline Flentge
a6963.title: WFP Deputy Country Director in Mali
a6963.speech: "In a complex humanitarian context where nearly 1.5 million people face acute food insecurity during this agro-pastoral lean season, the impact of the Kingdom of Spain's contributions will be all the more remarkable. Thanks to your generosity, in 2024 we were able to provide vital assistance to more than 50,000 vulnerable people across Mali. These are not mere statistics; they are families who were able to eat their fill, children who had access to the nutrition essential to grow and develop, and entire communities who saw their hope reborn in the face of the complex challenges of food insecurity."

a6963.speaker: Jacqueline Flentge, WFP Deputy Country Director in Mali
a6963.name: Jacqueline Flentge
a6963.title: WFP Deputy Country Director in Mali
a6963.speech: "Despite these significant advances made possible by partners such as Spain, the road to zero hunger is still long and strewn with obstacles. The challenges of financing humanitarian and development operations remain considerable, with needs that keep growing in the face of multiple crises. Every day we face the complexity of mobilising the resources needed to respond to the scale of needs in Mali." ; "In order to cover the essential needs of vulnerable communities over the next six months, the WFP urgently needs 91.4 million US dollars, or more than 50 billion CFA francs, by the end of December 2025. That is why the support of our partners is absolutely vital."

a6963.speaker: Jacqueline Flentge, WFP Deputy Country Director in Mali
a6963.name: Jacqueline Flentge
a6963.title: WFP Deputy Country Director in Mali
a6963.speech: "I also wish to reiterate the WFP's firm commitment to continue working hand in hand with the Food Security Commission for the effective implementation of the national food security policy. We are determined to strengthen our actions in the field, to innovate in our approaches and to reach the most vulnerable populations. We are convinced that it is by joining forces, sharing our expertise and mobilising the necessary resources that we will be able to make lasting progress towards a Mali free of hunger."

a7056.speaker: Johannes Mururani, participant in the Commitment Walk
a7056.name: Johannes Mururani
a7056.title: participant in the Commitment Walk
a7056.speech: Told the group he was a violent man until he attended a male engagement program on gender norms under the USAID Reach Namibia Project, and that he is now adamant about creating a safe environment. “Imagine a world where boys and girls can walk safely to school without fear of violence. A world where women can make decisions about their health and bodies without coercion. A world where men and women stand together as equals, united in the fight against gender-based violence and HIV.”

a7056.speaker: Katamba Nanyemba, Project Coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project
a7056.name: Katamba Nanyemba
a7056.title: Project Coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project
a7056.speech: Says the link between gender-based violence and HIV is well documented. “It shows us that survivors of violence have often limited control over their sexual health, face power imbalances that prevent them from negotiating safer sex, and fear stigma that deters them from accessing critical services.”

a7056.speaker: Bonifatius Wakudumo, Kavango East Governor
a7056.name: Bonifatius Wakudumo
a7056.title: Kavango East Governor
a7056.speech: Told the group that it is their duty as men to educate themselves and others about GBV, its root causes, and its impact on individuals. “It is believed that five in six men are not abusers. But where are they? Can they stand up and be counted? Can the one in six who are abusers change their ways? Can we raise a new generation based on equality? Change is not easy, and it does not happen overnight. But every step we take today is a step toward building a safer and more equitable future. Let us be unwavering in our commitment and courageous in our actions.”

a7244.speaker: John Nyawali, Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) Spokesperson
a7244.name: John Nyawali
a7244.title: Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) Spokesperson
a7244.speech: Confirmed to ZNBC News in Lusaka that the DEC had seized two motor vehicles belonging to Christine Kaseba, wife of Patriotic Front leader Michael Sata ; said the vehicles were taken to the DEC headquarters this morning by Mr. Sata's drivers and lawyers ; said that Mr. Sata, through his lawyers, was asked to surrender the two motor vehicles which are a subject of investigations to the Commission after recording a second statement from him.

a7330.speaker: "Alafia 2025" national vision document (Benin)
a7330.name: "Alafia 2025" national vision document (Benin)
a7330.speech: Provides for making Benin "a beacon country, well governed, united and peaceful, with a prosperous and competitive economy, cultural influence and social well-being"; sets out the desiderata of the Beninese over a twenty-five year period.

a7409.speaker: Daouda Mariko, director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.name: Daouda Mariko
a7409.title: director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.speech: “I wanted to be of service to my people; the written press was not really the convincing medium at the time. Radio had more impact on behaviour change for informing the population than the written press.”

a7409.speaker: Daouda Mariko, director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.name: Daouda Mariko
a7409.title: director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.speech: “I do not carry out any activities outside radio. I have done training courses and internships in which I specialised in order to deepen my skills.”

a7409.speaker: Daouda Mariko, director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.name: Daouda Mariko
a7409.title: director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.speech: “I had the chance to train practically all the radio stations set up by USAID. I also do consultancies for the training of radio stations, for American NGOs, in Niger and Chad.”

a7409.speaker: Daouda Mariko, director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.name: Daouda Mariko
a7409.title: director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.speech: “Our programme on women promotes women, with debates on couples’ problems, which was appreciated by men; some bought radios for their wives and encouraged them to give their point of view; and the programme on the economic panorama (on the small number of women with access to credit lines) for foreign investors, so that they can be agents of development.”

a7409.speaker: Daouda Mariko, director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.name: Daouda Mariko
a7409.title: director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.speech: “Through our programmes, our listeners in Burkina created the Radio Kénédougou Listeners’ Club. It is a mechanism that helps a great deal in criticising the programmes in order to improve the quality of the presenters, and the signal when the frequency is poor in a locality.”

a7409.speaker: Daouda Mariko, director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.name: Daouda Mariko
a7409.title: director/promoter of Radio Kénédougou in Sikasso
a7409.speech: Advises young journalists of all categories to be professional, to do their research and to advocate excellence for better performance: “We are in international competition; Mali has always been among the leaders. In the future, we must fear that the country may be entrusted to people who have no capacity or intellectual competence. As for radio, it must be noted that a radio station is nothing without its listeners; I thank them from the bottom of my heart for this trust, as well as the UJRM, which chose me to sponsor the Sikasso 2024 regional tour.”

a7423.speaker: Mariatou Koné, Minister of National Education and Literacy of Côte d’Ivoire
a7423.name: Mariatou Koné
a7423.title: Minister of National Education and Literacy of Côte d’Ivoire
a7423.speech: Assured that the SIGE is a “robust and wise” instrument that “embodies an ambitious and shared vision” of effective, transparent educational governance based on reliable data ; declared that this integrated national system, capable of “collecting, processing and analysing educational data, is a major step forward” in a context marked by digital transformation and the growing demand for performance ; said the solution responds to a “pressing” need, namely having reliable educational data in real time, indispensable for strategic decision-making to improve the education system ; explained: “Thanks to the SIGE, our ministry will be able to rigorously monitor the schooling of children across the whole national territory, better plan the construction of school infrastructure, and allocate human and material resources more equitably and more efficiently” ; maintained: “The SIGE is not only a software solution, but a strategic lever serving a modern, integrated, responsive and proactive steering of education and a concrete response to the management challenges faced by the Ivorian education system” ; said the platform will “simplify and optimise” administrative, pedagogical and logistical operations within schools while facilitating the “smooth” flow of information between the different levels ; said the tool should prepare a “more rigorous, responsive and more effective” management of the education system and provide disaggregated indicators accessible in real time ; affirmed it will facilitate resource planning, monitoring of the implementation of education policies, evaluation of their impact and the ministry’s capacity to account precisely and transparently for its actions ; added: “By facilitating the exchange of structured information, the traceability of correspondence and the harmonisation of standards, they will allow better inter-institutional coordination around the educational, social and professional pathways of pupils and teachers” ; assured that the system’s functionalities were tested in schools in the regions of Bouaké (centre) and San Pedro (south-west) ; said the handover of the SIGE is an “achievement, but above all a starting point” and that the challenge now is to ensure its effective ownership by all actors in the Ivorian education system.

a7423.speaker: Mariatou Koné, Minister of National Education and Literacy of Côte d’Ivoire
a7423.name: Mariatou Koné
a7423.title: Minister of National Education and Literacy of Côte d’Ivoire
a7423.speech: Launched an appeal to the Ministry of Finance and Budget, to bilateral and multilateral partners and to the private sector for complementary financing with a view to extending the SIGE to all schools and regional directorates.

a7423.speaker: Jessica Davis Ba, United States Ambassador to Côte d’Ivoire
a7423.name: Jessica Davis Ba
a7423.title: United States Ambassador to Côte d’Ivoire
a7423.speech: Recalled that the SIGE is the fruit of the partnership between her country and Côte d’Ivoire, through the Compact programme financed by the Millennium Challenge Account-Côte d’Ivoire ; welcomed this system, which represents an “instrument of transparency, accountability, performance and innovation”, offering the Ivorian state the means to better plan, better manage and better decide for the future of Ivorian schooling.
